title.zh: 卷三百二十八 列傳第八十七 李清臣 安燾 張璪 蒲宗孟 黃履 蔡挺 王韶 薛向 章楶
title.en: Volume 328 Biographies 87: Li Qingchen, An Dao, Zhang Zao, Pu Zongmeng, Huang Lu, Cai Ting, Wang Shao, Xue Xiang, Zhang Jie
title.raw: 卷三百二十八 列傳第八十七 李清臣 安燾 張璪 蒲宗孟 黃履 蔡挺 王韶 薛向 章楶 Volume 328 Biographies 87: Li Qingchen, An Dao, Zhang Zao, Pu Zongmeng, Huang Lu, Cai Ting, Wang Shao, Xue Xiang, Zhang Jie

sentences.zh: 李清臣

translations.literal: Li Qingchen
translations.idiomatic: Li Qingchen

sentences.zh: 李清臣，字邦直，魏人也。

translations.literal: Li Qingchen, style name Bangzhi, was a man of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qingchen, courtesy name Bangzhi, was a native of Wei.

sentences.zh: 七歲知讀書，日數千言，暫經目輒誦，稍能戲為文章。

translations.literal: At age seven he knew how to read; each day he went through several thousand words; what briefly passed before his eyes he could recite; he could also somewhat play at composing essays.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could read; each day he worked through thousands of characters, and whatever he briefly glanced at he could recite from memory; he could also compose essays with some ease.

sentences.zh: 客有從京師來者，與其兄談佛寺火，清臣從傍應曰：「此所謂災也，或者其蠹民已甚，天固儆之邪？

translations.literal: A guest who had come from the capital was speaking with his elder brother about a fire at a Buddhist temple; Qingchen responded from the side: "This is what is called a calamity—perhaps they have harmed the people excessively, and Heaven is surely warning them, is it not?"
translations.idiomatic: A visitor from the capital was discussing a temple fire with his elder brother when Qingchen chimed in from the side: "This is what people call a disaster—perhaps the monks have preyed on the people too long, and Heaven is sending a warning?"

sentences.zh: 」因作《浮圖災解》。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he composed "An Explanation of the Buddhist-Temple Calamity."
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote an essay entitled "On the Calamity of Buddhist Pagodas."

sentences.zh: 兄驚曰：「是必大吾門。

translations.literal: His brother said in astonishment: "This one is sure to enlarge our house."
translations.idiomatic: His brother exclaimed in amazement, "This boy will surely bring great honor to our family."

sentences.zh: 」韓琦聞其名，以兄之子妻之。

translations.literal: " When Han Qi heard his name, he gave him his nephew's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi heard of him, he gave Qingchen his nephew's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調邢州司戶參軍、和川令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Revenue Section aide at Xingzhou and magistrate of Hechuan.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he was posted as revenue clerk at Xingzhou and magistrate of Hechuan.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，薦者逾十數，應得京官。

translations.literal: When his term was complete, more than ten people recommended him; he was due to receive a capital-office appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, more than ten sponsors recommended him, and he was eligible for promotion to a capital post.

sentences.zh: 適舉將薛向有公事未竟，閡銓格，判銓張掞擿使自陳勿用。

translations.literal: It happened that Xue Xiang of the presenting office had unfinished official business, which blocked the examination regulations; Zhang Shan, who adjudicated the board, picked at the matter and had him state that he should not be used.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xue Xiang, who was to present the nomination, still had unfinished official business, which blocked the personnel rules; Zhang Shan, chief examiner of the board, seized on the point and had Qingchen declare that he should not be appointed.

sentences.zh: 清臣曰：「人以家保己而己舍之，薄矣。

translations.literal: Qingchen said: "When others use their household connections to protect themselves but one abandons them, that is mean."
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen said, "When others rely on family ties to protect themselves, it would be petty of me to abandon them."

sentences.zh: 願待之。

translations.literal: I wish to wait for him.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather wait for him.

sentences.zh: 」掞離席曰：「君能如是，未可量也。

translations.literal: " Shan rose from his seat and said: "If you can act like this, your measure cannot yet be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shan rose from his seat and said, "A man who can act as you do cannot yet be measured."

sentences.zh: 」應材識兼茂科，歐陽修壯其文，以比蘇軾。

translations.literal: " He responded to the Exceptional Talent and Outstanding Ability examination; Ouyang Xiu was impressed with his writing and compared him to Su Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Exceptional Talent and Outstanding Ability examination; Ouyang Xiu admired his prose and compared him to Su Shi.

sentences.zh: 治平二年，試秘閣，考官韓維曰：「荀卿氏筆力也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiping, he took the Secret Pavilion examination; examining official Han Wei said: "This is Xun Qing's writing power."
translations.idiomatic: In 1065 he sat for the Secret Pavilion examination. Examiner Han Wei remarked, "This is the pen of Xunzi himself."

sentences.zh: 」試文至中書，修迎語曰：「不置李清臣於第一，則謬矣。

translations.literal: When the examination papers reached the Central Secretariat, Xiu greeted them and said: "If Li Qingchen is not placed first, then it would be erroneous."
translations.idiomatic: When the papers reached the Central Secretariat, Ouyang Xiu greeted the examiners and said, "It would be absurd not to place Li Qingchen first."

sentences.zh: 」啟視如言。

translations.literal: Upon opening and viewing, it was as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: When they opened the papers and reviewed them, it proved exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 時大雨霖，災異數見，論者歸咎濮議。

translations.literal: At that time there was heavy prolonged rain; calamities and anomalies appeared repeatedly; commentators attributed blame to the Pu discussion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time torrential rains persisted and portents multiplied; commentators blamed the controversy over Emperor Yingzong's natural father.

sentences.zh: 及廷對，或謂曰：「宜以《五行傳》『簡宗廟，水不潤下』為證，必擢上第。

translations.literal: When it came to the palace examination, someone said to him: "You should use as evidence from the Treatise on the Five Phases, 'When ancestral temples are curtailed, water fails to descend'—this will surely gain the top rank."
translations.idiomatic: When the palace examination came, someone advised him: "You should cite the Treatise on the Five Phases—'When ancestral temples are curtailed, water fails to descend'—as proof; that will surely win you the highest honors."

sentences.zh: 」清臣曰：「此漢儒附會之說也，吾不之信。

translations.literal: Qingchen said: "This is the forced correlation of Han Confucians—I do not believe it. Are there not grievances and sufferings among the people that could be reported upward?"
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen replied, "That is a forced reading by Han scholastics—I do not accept it. Surely there are grievances among the people worthy of being brought before the throne?"

sentences.zh: 民間豈無疾痛可上者乎？

translations.literal: Are there not grievances and sufferings among the people that could be reported upward?
translations.idiomatic: Surely there are grievances among the people worthy of being brought before the throne?

sentences.zh: 」即條對言：「天地之大，譬如人一身，腹心肺腑有所攻塞，則五官為之不寧。

translations.literal: Immediately he responded item by item, saying: "Heaven and earth in their vastness are like a single human body; when the belly, heart, lungs, and viscera suffer obstruction, then the five sense organs are thereby unsettled."
translations.idiomatic: He then answered point by point: "Heaven and earth in their immensity are like a single body; when the belly, heart, and lungs are obstructed, the five senses grow restless."

sentences.zh: 民人生聚，天地之腹心肺腑也；

translations.literal: The people's living and gathering are heaven and earth's belly, heart, lungs, and viscera;
translations.idiomatic: The living masses of the people are the belly and heart of heaven and earth;

sentences.zh: 日月星辰，天地之五官也。

translations.literal: The sun, moon, and stars are heaven and earth's five sense organs.
translations.idiomatic: The sun, moon, and stars are heaven and earth's five senses.

sentences.zh: 善止天地之異者，不止其異，止民之疾痛而已。

translations.literal: One who skillfully stops heaven and earth's anomalies does not merely stop the anomalies—he only stops the people's grievances and sufferings.
translations.idiomatic: To truly quell the signs of heaven and earth, one does not suppress the portents themselves but relieves the people's suffering.

sentences.zh: 」策入等，以秘書郎簽書平江軍判官，名聲籍甚。

translations.literal: His policy essay entered the grades; he was appointed as secretary and signing military judge at Pingjiang Circuit; his fame was greatly renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His examination essay placed among the top ranks, and he was appointed secretary and signing military judge at Pingjiang Circuit; his reputation soared.

sentences.zh: 英宗知之，語王廣淵曰：「韓琦固忠臣，但避嫌太審。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong knew of this and said to Wang Guangyuan: "Han Qi is indeed a loyal minister, but he is too careful in avoiding suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong took note and said to Wang Guangyuan, "Han Qi is a loyal minister, to be sure, but he is excessively cautious about avoiding suspicion.

sentences.zh: 如李清臣者，公議皆謂可用，顧以親抑之可乎？

translations.literal: As for someone like Li Qingchen, public consensus all says he can be used—yet to suppress him because of kinship, can that be acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone like Li Qingchen is widely regarded as fit for office—can we really hold him back merely because he is a relative?"

sentences.zh: 」既而詔舉館閣，歐陽修薦之，得集賢校理、同知太常禮院。

translations.literal: Shortly after, an edict summoned candidates for the Hall and Pavilion; Ouyang Xiu recommended him; he obtained the posts of collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and associate director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict called for nominations to the Academies; Ouyang Xiu recommended him, and he was appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and associate director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時熙、豐法度，一切厘正，清臣固爭之，罷為資政殿學士、知河陽，徙河南、永興。

translations.literal: At that time the Xining and Yuanfeng laws and institutions were being entirely rectified; Qingchen firmly contested this; he was dismissed as academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and made prefect of Heyang; he was transferred to Henan and Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xining and Yuanfeng reforms were being systematically overhauled, Qingchen objected strenuously and was removed, made academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Heyang, then transferred to Henan and Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 召為吏部尚書，給事中姚勔駁之，改知真定府。

translations.literal: He was summoned as minister of the Ministry of Personnel; supervising secretariat drafter Yao Miao rejected it; he was changed to prefect of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as minister of personnel, but drafting reviewer Yao Miao blocked the appointment; the emperor reassigned him as prefect of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 班行有王宗正者，致憾於故帥，使其妻詣使者，告前後饋餉過制，囚繫數百人。

translations.literal: Among the official ranks there was one Wang Zongzheng who harbored resentment toward the former prefect; he had his wife go to the imperial messenger and report that gifts and provisions before and after exceeded regulations; several hundred people were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk named Wang Zongzheng, nursing a grudge against the former prefect, sent his wife to denounce him to the imperial envoy for repeatedly giving gifts beyond what regulations allowed; several hundred people were thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 清臣至，立奏解其獄，而竄宗正。

translations.literal: When Qingchen arrived, he immediately memorialized to release the prisoners, and Wang Zongzheng was banished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingchen took up the post, he immediately petitioned to free them and had Wang Zongzheng exiled.

sentences.zh: 帝親政，拜中書侍郎，勔復駁之，不聽。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally took charge of government, Qingchen was appointed vice director of the Central Secretariat; Miao again rejected it; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor began to rule in his own right, Qingchen was appointed vice director of the Secretariat; Yao Miao objected again, but the emperor overruled him.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，廷試進士，清臣發策曰：「今復詞賦之選而士不知勸，罷常平之官而農不加富，可差可募之說雜而役法病，或東或北之論異而河患滋，賜土以柔遠也而羌夷之患未弭，弛利以便民也而商賈之路不通。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, at the palace examination for jinshi, Qingchen issued the policy question, saying: "Now poetry and prose selection is restored yet scholars are not encouraged; Ever-Normal Granary officials are abolished yet farmers are not enriched; theories of corvée labor and hired labor mingle and the corvée law is afflicted; eastern and northern theories differ and river calamities increase; granting land to pacify distant peoples yet Qiang and barbarian troubles are not quelled; relaxing profit restrictions to benefit the people yet merchants' routes are not opened."
translations.idiomatic: In 1094, at the palace examination for new jinshi, Qingchen set the policy question: "Poetry and prose have been restored to the examinations, yet scholars are not motivated to excel; Ever-Normal Granary offices have been abolished, yet farmers are no richer; debate over corvée and hired labor has muddied the labor-service law; conflicting plans for the Yellow River only worsen its floods; land grants meant to pacify frontier peoples have not stilled Qiang and tribal unrest; and easing commercial restrictions to help the people has failed to open trade routes."

sentences.zh: 夫可則因，否則革，惟當之為貴，聖人亦何有必焉。

translations.literal: What can be done, then follow; what cannot, then reform—only what is fitting is prized; even sages have nothing they must insist upon.
translations.idiomatic: What works should be kept; what fails should be changed—fitness is all that matters, and even sages impose no fixed dogma.

sentences.zh: 」主意皆絀元祐之政，策士悟其指，於是紹述之論大興，國是遂變。

translations.literal: The intent was entirely to discredit Yuanyou policies; examination candidates grasped his meaning; thus the theory of continuing the legacy greatly flourished, and the national standard thereafter changed.
translations.idiomatic: The thrust of the questions was to repudiate Yuanyou policy; candidates grasped the hint, the "continuing the legacy" movement surged, and the direction of the state shifted.

sentences.zh: 范純仁去位，清臣獨顓中書，亟復青苗、免役法，除諸路提舉官。

translations.literal: Fan Chunren left his post; Qingchen alone headed the Central Secretariat; he hastily restored the Green Sprouts and Corvée Exemption laws and appointed supervising officials in each circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After Fan Chunren left office, Qingchen held sole sway at the Secretariat; he quickly restored the Green Sprouts and Corvée Exemption laws and appointed circuit-wide supervising commissioners.

sentences.zh: 覬為相，顧蘇轍軋己，乃擿轍嘗以漢武比先帝激上怒，轍罷。

translations.literal: Coveting the chancellorship, but seeing Su Zhe obstruct him, he then picked at the fact that Zhe had once compared the Former Emperor to Emperor Wu of Han, arousing the emperor's anger; Zhe was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Ambitious for the prime ministership but blocked by Su Zhe, he seized on Zhe's past comparison of the late emperor to Emperor Wu of Han, provoking the throne's wrath; Zhe was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 時召章惇未至，清臣心益覬之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Dun had been summoned but had not yet arrived; Qingchen's heart coveted the post all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun had been recalled but had not yet arrived, and Qingchen's ambition for the chancellorship burned brighter.

sentences.zh: 已而惇入相，復與為異。

translations.literal: Before long Dun entered the chancellorship; again they were at odds.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun finally took office as chancellor, the two men soon fell out again.

sentences.zh: 惇既逐諸臣，並籍文彥博、呂公著以下三十人，將悉竄嶺表。

translations.literal: After Dun had driven out various ministers, he also registered Wen Yanbo, Lü Gongzhu, and thirty others below them, intending to banish them all beyond the Lingnan region.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Dun purged a host of officials, he drew up a list of Wen Yanbo, Lü Gongzhu, and thirty others, intending to exile them all to the far south.

sentences.zh: 清臣曰：「更先帝法度，不為無過，然皆累朝元老，若從惇言，必大駭物聽。

translations.literal: Qingchen said: "Altering the Former Emperor's laws and institutions is not without fault, yet all are veterans of successive reigns; if we follow Dun's words, it will greatly shock public opinion."
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen said, "Changing the late emperor's institutions was not without fault, but these men are elders who served many reigns; if we follow Zhang Dun's advice, we will deeply alarm the realm."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「是豈無中道耶？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Is there not a middle way in this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Surely there is a moderate course?"

sentences.zh: 合揭榜朝堂，置餘人不問。

translations.literal: Post the list in the court hall and leave the rest unprosecuted."
translations.idiomatic: Post the list in the court hall but leave the others alone."

sentences.zh: 」鄜延路金明砦主將張興戰沒，惇怒，議盡戮全軍四千人。

translations.literal: At Fuyan Circuit, Jinming Stockade commander-in-chief Zhang Xing died in battle; Dun was furious and proposed executing the entire army of four thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xing, garrison commander at Jinming Stockade on the Fuyan frontier, fell in battle, Zhang Dun flew into a rage and proposed putting the entire four-thousand-man garrison to the sword.

sentences.zh: 清臣曰：「將死亦多端，或先登爭利，或輕身入敵。

translations.literal: Qingchen said: "Generals die in many ways—some lead the assault competing for merit, some throw themselves lightly into the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen objected, "Generals die in many ways—some storm the walls seeking glory, others throw themselves recklessly at the foe.

sentences.zh: 今悉誅吏士，異時亡將必舉軍降虜矣。

translations.literal: If now all officers and soldiers are executed, in future when a general dies, the army will surely surrender en masse to the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Execute every man now, and the next time a commander falls, his troops will surrender wholesale to the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」於是但誅牙兵十六輩。

translations.literal: Thereupon only sixteen guard soldiers were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end only sixteen personal guards were put to death.

sentences.zh: 上幸楚王第，有狂婦人遮道叫呼，告清臣謀反，屬吏捕治，本澶州娼而為清臣姑子田氏外婦者。

translations.literal: The emperor visited the Prince of Chu's residence; a mad woman blocked the road shouting, accusing Qingchen of plotting rebellion; subordinate officials arrested and investigated her; she was originally a courtesan from Cangzhou and was the extramarital consort of Tian, Qingchen's nephew by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Prince of Chu's mansion, a deranged woman blocked the road crying that Qingchen was plotting rebellion. Officials seized her and discovered she was a former Cangzhou prostitute and the mistress of Qingchen's nephew by marriage, surnamed Tian.

sentences.zh: 清臣不能引去，用御史言，以大學士知河南，尋落職知真定府。

translations.literal: Qingchen could not withdraw on his own; following the censor's recommendation, he was made grand academician and prefect of Henan; shortly he was demoted and made prefect of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to resign of his own accord, Qingchen, on the censors' advice, was transferred as grand academician and prefect of Henan; soon he was stripped of his academy title and reassigned to Zhending.

sentences.zh: 初，蔡確子渭上書訴父冤，造奇譖以陷劉摯罪，清臣心知其誣，弗之省，坐奪學士。

translations.literal: Initially, Cai Que's son Wei submitted a memorial pleading his father's innocence, fabricating bizarre slanders to trap Liu Zhe in guilt; Qingchen in his heart knew it was false but did not investigate; he was punished by loss of his academician title.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cai Que's son Wei had petitioned to clear his father's name, inventing outlandish charges to frame Liu Zhe; Qingchen knew the accusations were bogus but failed to look into them, and lost his academy title as punishment.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，入為門下侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended, he entered office as vice director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne, Qingchen was recalled as vice director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 僕射韓忠彥與之有連，惟其言是聽，出范純禮、張舜民，不使呂希純、劉安世入朝，皆其謀也。

translations.literal: Grand Counselor Han Zhongyan was connected with him; only his words were heeded; Fan Chunli and Zhang Shunmin were removed; Lü Xichun and Liu Anshi were not allowed to enter court—all were his schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Counselor Han Zhongyan was allied with him; the emperor listened only to his counsel; Fan Chunli and Zhang Shunmin were ousted, and Lü Xichun and Liu Anshi were kept from court—all at his instigation.

sentences.zh: 尋為曾布所陷，出知大名府而卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: Shortly he was trapped by Zeng Bu, sent out as prefect of Daming and died there, age seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zeng Bu brought him down; he was sent out as prefect of Daming and died there at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 清臣蚤以詞藻受知神宗，建大理寺，築都城，皆命作記，簡重宏放，文體各成一家。

translations.literal: Qingchen early by literary talent received Shenzong's recognition; building the Court of Judicial Review, constructing the capital city—both were ordered for him to compose records; his style was concise, weighty, grand and unrestrained; each literary form became a school of its own.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen won Shenzong's favor early for his literary gifts; he was commissioned to write the commemorative records for the new Court of Judicial Review and the capital walls—prose at once terse, weighty, and expansive, each piece a distinct achievement.

sentences.zh: 為人寬洪，不忮害。

translations.literal: As a person he was broad and magnanimous, not jealous or harmful.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous by nature and free of malice.

sentences.zh: 嘗為舒亶所劾，及在尚書，亶以贓抵罪，獨申救之，曰：「亶信亡狀，然謂之贓則不可。

translations.literal: He was once impeached by Shu Dan; when he was at the Ministry, Dan was convicted of embezzlement; Qingchen alone pleaded to save him, saying: "Dan's conduct was indeed reprehensible, yet to call it embezzlement is not acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Shu Dan had once impeached him; later, when Qingchen headed the Ministry of Personnel, Dan was convicted of corruption, and Qingchen alone interceded: "Dan's conduct was indeed reprehensible, but to call it graft goes too far.

sentences.zh: 」再為姚勔所駁，當紹聖議貶，或激使甘心，清臣為之言曰：「勔以職事，所見或不同，豈應以臣故而加重？

translations.literal: Again rejected by Yao Miao; when Shaosheng deliberated demotion, some incited to make him bear it willingly; Qingchen spoke on his behalf: "Miao in his official duties—views may differ—how should he be punished more heavily because of me?"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Miao had twice blocked his appointments; during the Shaosheng purges some urged heavier punishment for Miao, but Qingchen spoke up: "Miao was performing his duty; officials may disagree—why should he be punished more severely on my account?"

sentences.zh: 」帝悟，薄勔罪。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and lightened Miao's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the point and mitigated Yao Miao's sentence.

sentences.zh: 起身窮約，以儉自持，至富貴不改。

translations.literal: Rising from poverty and hardship, he maintained himself through frugality; even upon reaching wealth and honor he did not change.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from poverty and practiced thrift throughout; even in high office he did not change his ways.

sentences.zh: 居官奉法，毋敢撓以私。

translations.literal: In office he followed the law; he did not dare bend it for private reasons.
translations.idiomatic: In office he upheld the law and never bent it for private ends.

sentences.zh: 然志在利祿，不公於謀國，一意欲取宰相，故操持悖謬，竟不如願以死。

translations.literal: Yet his ambition lay in profit and emolument; he was not impartial in planning for the state; single-mindedly he wished to seize the chancellorship; therefore his conduct was perverse and absurd; in the end he did not obtain his wish and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was driven by appetite for rank and emolument, not impartial counsel for the realm; obsessed with the prime ministership, his judgment grew reckless, and he died without ever attaining it.

sentences.zh: 後朝議以復孟后罪，追貶武安軍節度副使，再貶雷州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Later the court deliberated on restoring Empress Meng's grievance; he was posthumously demoted to military commissioner deputy of Wu'an Army; again demoted to revenue section aide at Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: A later court, revisiting the wrong done to Empress Meng, posthumously demoted him to deputy military commissioner of Wu'an and then again to revenue clerk at Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 安燾，字厚卿，開封人。

translations.literal: An Tao, style name Houqing, was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: An Tao, courtesy name Houqing, was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 幼警悟。

translations.literal: In youth he was precocious and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was exceptionally bright.

sentences.zh: 年十一，從學里中，羞與群兒伍，聞有老先生聚徒，往師之。

translations.literal: At age eleven, studying in the village, he was ashamed to rank with the herd of children; hearing there was an old master gathering disciples, he went to take him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven, while studying locally, he was reluctant to mingle with ordinary boys; learning that an elder scholar nearby was taking disciples, he went to seek instruction.

sentences.zh: 先生曰：「汝方為誦數之學，未可從吾遊，當群試省題一詩，中選乃置汝。

translations.literal: The master said: "You are still at the level of recitation and counting learning; you are not yet fit to follow me; when the group tries a provincial examination topic with one poem, if selected then I will accept you."
translations.idiomatic: The master told him, "You are still learning rote and arithmetic; you are not ready to study with me. Compose a poem on the provincial examination topic with the other students—if yours is chosen, I will take you in.

sentences.zh: 」燾無難色。

translations.literal: Tao showed no difficulty in expression.
translations.idiomatic: An Tao did not hesitate.

sentences.zh: 詩成，出諸生上，由是知名。

translations.literal: When the poem was complete, it surpassed the other students'; thereby he became known.
translations.idiomatic: His poem ranked above every other student's, and his name spread from that day.

sentences.zh: 登第，調蔡州觀察推官，至太常丞、主管大名府路機宜文字。

translations.literal: He passed the examination; appointed investigating prefectural aide at Caizhou; rose to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and supervisor of strategic documents for Daming Prefecture Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the examinations he was posted as judicial aide at Caizhou, eventually rising to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and supervisor of strategic documents on the Daming Circuit staff.

sentences.zh: 用歐陽修薦，為秘閣校理、判吏部南曹、荊湖北路轉運判官、提點刑獄兼常平、農田水利、差役事。

translations.literal: On Ouyang Xiu's recommendation, he became Secret Pavilion collator, adjudicator of the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, transport commissioner judge for Jinghu North Circuit, and judicial intendant concurrently overseeing Ever-Normal Granary, agricultural fields and waterworks, and corvée labor affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On Ouyang Xiu's recommendation he was appointed Secret Pavilion collator, concurrent reviewer in the Ministry of Personnel's southern bureau, transport judge on the Jinghu North Circuit, and judicial intendant with oversight of Ever-Normal Granary, irrigation, and corvée policy.

sentences.zh: 時方興新法，奉行之吏，或迎合求進。

translations.literal: At that time the New Policies were being launched; officials implementing them sometimes catered to gain advancement.
translations.idiomatic: The New Policies were just being rolled out, and some implementing officials curried favor to win promotion.

sentences.zh: 司農符檄日夜下，如免役增寬剩，造簿供手實，青苗責保任，追胥苛切，其類旁午。

translations.literal: Ministry of Revenue documents and orders descended day and night—such as corvée exemption increasing surplus reserves, compiling registers and supplying household reports, Green Sprouts loans demanding guarantors, tax collectors harsh and cutting—the categories crisscrossed.
translations.idiomatic: Orders from the Ministry of Revenue poured in night and day—extra corvée quotas, surplus-tax levies, household-property registers, Green Sprouts guarantors, brutal collection agents—one mandate piled on another.

sentences.zh: 燾平心奉法，列其泰甚於朝。

translations.literal: Tao with even mind followed the law; he listed the most excessive items before the court.
translations.idiomatic: An Tao enforced the law evenhandedly and memorialized the worst abuses to court.

sentences.zh: 移使京東路，過闕入見，神宗偉其儀觀，留檢正中書孔目房、修起居注。

translations.literal: Transferred as envoy to Jingdong Circuit; passing the capital he entered for audience; Shenzong admired his bearing and appearance; he was retained to check and rectify the Central Secretariat clerks' office and compile the Diary of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Jingdong circuit, he stopped at court for an audience; Shenzong was impressed by his bearing and kept him to audit the Secretariat clerks' office and compile the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，高麗新通使，假燾左諫議大夫往報之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfeng, Goryeo newly sent envoys; Tao was temporarily given the title Left Remonstrance Grand Counselor to go respond.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuanfeng era, when Goryeo reopened diplomatic contact, An Tao was temporarily appointed Left Remonstrance Grand Counselor and dispatched in reply.

sentences.zh: 高麗迎勞，館餼加契丹禮數等，使近臣言：「王遇使者甚敬，出誠心，非若奉契丹苟免邊患而已。

translations.literal: Goryeo welcomed and entertained him; hosting and provisions matched Khitan ceremonial standards; an envoy close minister said: "The king treats the emissary with great respect, showing genuine sincerity—not like serving the Khitan merely to escape border troubles."
translations.idiomatic: The Goryeo court received him with honors and hospitality matching Khitan protocol; a royal confidant explained, "Our king welcomes your envoy with true respect—it is not the grudging courtesy we show Khitan envoys merely to keep the border quiet.

sentences.zh: 」燾笑答曰：「尊中華，事大國，禮一也，特以罕至有加爾。

translations.literal: Tao smiled and replied: "Honoring China and serving a great state—the ritual is one; only because visits are rare is there extra courtesy."
translations.idiomatic: An Tao smiled and replied, "Respect for China and deference to a great power follow the same protocol; you simply add ceremony because our missions are rare.

sentences.zh: 朝廷與遼國通好久，豈復於此較厚薄哉！

translations.literal: The court has maintained relations with Liao for long—how could we still compare thick and thin here!"
translations.idiomatic: Our court has exchanged envoys with Liao for generations—surely we no longer bother to weigh who shows more favor!"

sentences.zh: 」使還，帝以為知禮，即授所假官，兼直學士院。

translations.literal: Upon return, the emperor considered him knowledgeable in ritual, immediately granted the temporarily lent office, concurrently Academy Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, the emperor judged him skilled in diplomacy and confirmed his temporary appointment while adding membership in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 知審刑院，決剖滯訟五百餘案。

translations.literal: Directed the Court for Judicial Review; decided and adjudicated over five hundred backlog cases.
translations.idiomatic: As head of the Court for Judicial Review he cleared more than five hundred backlogged cases.

sentences.zh: 因言：「每蔽獄上省，輕重有疑，則必致駁，勢既不敵，故法官顧避稽停。

translations.literal: He therefore said: "Whenever closed cases are sent up to the Secretariat, if severity or leniency is doubtful, rejection is sure to follow; when momentum is unmatched, therefore judicial officials look back and avoid, delaying and stopping."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Whenever a decided case goes up to the Secretariat, any dispute over severity draws a reversal; outmatched, judges hold back and cases stall.

sentences.zh: 請自今以疑獄讞者，皆得輕論。

translations.literal: I request from now that those who adjudicate doubtful cases may all argue for leniency."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter judges may always recommend the lighter penalty when a case is doubtful.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 求知陳州，還，為龍圖閣直學士、判軍器監。

translations.literal: Requested to know Chen Prefecture; returned, became Hanlin Academician of Dragon Diagram Hall and director of the Directorate of Armaments.
translations.idiomatic: He requested assignment as prefect of Chenzhou; on returning to court he was made Hanlin academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and director of the Armaments Directorate.

sentences.zh: 命館遼使。

translations.literal: Ordered to host the Liao envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to host the Liao envoy.

sentences.zh: 方宴近郊，使者不令其徒分坐廡下，力爭之，使無以奪。

translations.literal: Just as a banquet was held in the near suburbs, the envoy would not allow his followers to sit separately in the corridor; Tao contested forcefully; the envoy had no means to override.
translations.idiomatic: During a banquet in the outer suburbs, the envoy refused to let his retinue sit separately in the side halls; An Tao insisted, and the envoy could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 至肄儀將見，又不使綴行分班，使者入，餘皆坐門外，燾請令門見而出，眾始愧悔。

translations.literal: When rehearsing ceremony before the audience, again he would not allow them to fall into line by ranks; the envoy entered, the rest all sat outside the gate; Tao requested that they enter at the gate for audience and leave; the group then felt shame and regret.
translations.idiomatic: At the rehearsal for the imperial audience he again tried to keep the retinue from taking their proper places in procession; when the envoy went in alone and the rest were left outside the gate, An Tao insisted they enter and leave by the gate with proper ceremony—only then did they show shame and relent.

sentences.zh: 逮辭日，悉如儀。

translations.literal: When the day of farewell came, all followed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: By the day of departure, all ceremonial requirements were met.

sentences.zh: 或謂細故無足較，燾曰：「契丹喜嘗試人，其漸不可長也。

translations.literal: Some said minor matters were not worth disputing; Tao said: "The Khitan delight in testing people; such tendencies must not be allowed to grow."
translations.idiomatic: Some said these were trifles not worth fighting over; An Tao replied, "The Khitan love to probe for weakness; that habit must not be indulged.

sentences.zh: 」俄權三司使，改戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly after he acted as commissioner of the Three Fiscal Departments; changed to minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed acting commissioner of the Three Fiscal Departments, then minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 六年。

translations.literal: Sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng.

sentences.zh: 同知樞密院。

translations.literal: Vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 夏人款塞，乞還侵疆。

translations.literal: The Western Xia people opened the border pass and begged return of encroached territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut court opened the frontier passes and asked that seized territory be restored.

sentences.zh: 燾言：「地有非要害者固宜予，然羌情無厭，當使知吾宥過而息兵，不應示以厭兵之意。

translations.literal: Tao said: "Land that is not strategically vital may indeed be given; yet Qiang temperament is insatiable; they should be made to know we pardon faults and cease arms—not shown an attitude of war-weariness."
translations.idiomatic: An Tao argued, "Non-critical territory may rightly be returned, but the Tangut appetite is never sated; they must see that we grant clemency and stand down from war—not that we have grown weary of fighting.

sentences.zh: 」哲宗立，復仍前議，二府遂欲並棄熙河。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended, again the previous deliberation was followed; the Two Departments then wished to abandon Xihé entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong succeeded to the throne the old proposal resurfaced, and the two chief councils moved to abandon the entire Hexi frontier.

sentences.zh: 燾固爭之，曰：「自靈武而東，皆中國故地。

translations.literal: Tao firmly contended, saying: "From Lingwu eastward—all is China's former territory."
translations.idiomatic: An Tao objected strenuously: "From Lingwu eastward lies territory that was once ours.

sentences.zh: 先帝有此武功，今無故棄之，豈不取輕於外夷？

translations.literal: The Former Emperor had this military achievement; now without cause to abandon it—would this not invite contempt from outer barbarians?"
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor won this ground by force of arms; to surrender it without cause—would we not be scorned by the border peoples?"

sentences.zh: 」於是但以葭蘆等四砦歸之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon only the four forts of Jialu and the like were returned to them.
translations.idiomatic: In the end only Jialu and three other forts were returned to the Tanguts.

sentences.zh: 蔡確輩更用事，燾循循其間，不能有所建明。

translations.literal: Cai Que and his faction came to power again; Tao moved deferentially among them and could advance nothing of note.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Que and his allies regained influence, An Tao kept a circumspect distance and could put forward nothing of consequence.

sentences.zh: 元祐二年，進知院事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanyou, he was promoted to director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanyou (1087), he was promoted to director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時復洮、河，擒鬼章青宜結，二邊少清，而幷塞猶苦寇掠。

translations.literal: At the time Tao and He had been recovered and Chief Qingyijie of Gui Zhang captured; the two frontiers were somewhat calm, yet the border garrisons along Bing still suffered from raiding.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi had been retaken and the Qiang chief Qingyijie captured, bringing a measure of quiet to both frontiers—yet the garrison towns along the Shanxi border still endured constant raids.

sentences.zh: 燾言：「為國者不可好用兵，亦不可畏用兵，好則疲民，畏則遺患。

translations.literal: Tao said: "One who governs a state must neither love to use troops nor fear to use them; to love it exhausts the people, to fear it leaves troubles behind.
translations.idiomatic: An Tao argued, "A state must neither be eager for war nor afraid of it—eagerness exhausts the people, fear leaves trouble to fester.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷每戒疆吏，非舉國入寇毋得應之，則固畏用兵矣。

translations.literal: Now the court constantly admonishes frontier officials that unless the enemy invades with the whole nation they must not respond—this is plainly fearing to use troops.
translations.idiomatic: The court now repeatedly warns frontier officials not to respond unless the enemy mounts a full-scale invasion—that is already to fear war.

sentences.zh: 雖僅保障戍，實墮其計中，願復講攻擾之策。

translations.literal: Although we merely protect the garrisons, in fact we fall into their scheme; I wish to restore discussion of attack-and-harass strategy.
translations.idiomatic: We may think we are only holding the line, but in truth we play into their design; I ask that we revive the strategy of offensive raids and harassment.

sentences.zh: 且乾順幼豎，梁氏擅權，族黨酋渠多反側顧望。

translations.literal: Moreover Qianshun is a young ruler, the Liang clan monopolizes power, and many tribal chiefs and clan leaders waver and look about in indecision.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Emperor Qianshun is still a youth, the Liang clan holds power in its grip, and many tribal chiefs and clan leaders are divided and wavering.

sentences.zh: 若有以離間之，未必不回戈而復怨，此一奇也。

translations.literal: If we have means to sow discord among them, they may well turn their swords around and bear resentment anew—this would be one extraordinary stroke.
translations.idiomatic: If we can drive wedges among them, they may well turn on one another in renewed enmity—that would be a singular opportunity.

sentences.zh: 」其後夏人自相攜貳，使來修貢，悉如燾策。

translations.literal: " Afterward the Xia people turned against one another; envoys came to pay tribute—all exactly as Tao had strategized.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Tanguts fell to infighting among themselves and sent envoys to resume tribute—precisely as An Tao had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 宣仁太后患國用不足，頗裁冗費，宗室奉亦在議中。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren worried that state revenues were insufficient and considerably cut redundant expenditures; stipends for the imperial clan were also under discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren, troubled by insufficient state revenues, moved to cut wasteful spending; even the stipends paid to members of the imperial clan came under review.

sentences.zh: 燾諫曰：「陛下雖痛抑外家，以示至公，然此舉不可不深思而熟計。

translations.literal: Tao remonstrated: "Your Majesty, though you strictly restrain the maternal kindred to show utmost fairness, yet this measure cannot but be deeply pondered and carefully calculated.
translations.idiomatic: An Tao remonstrated, "Your Majesty may wish to restrain the empress's kin severely so as to show perfect impartiality, but this step deserves the deepest thought and the most careful reckoning.

sentences.zh: 」太后悟，遂止。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager understood and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager took his point and dropped the proposal.

sentences.zh: 大河北流，宰相主水官議，必欲回之東注。

translations.literal: The Yellow River flowed north; the chief councillor sided with the waterworks officials and insisted on diverting it eastward.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River was flowing northward; the chief councillor backed the hydraulic engineers and pressed to divert it back east.

sentences.zh: 燾以河流入濼淀，久必淤淺，恐河朔無以禦敵，遂上言曰：「自小吳未決之前，河雖屢徙，而盡在中國，故京師得以為北限。

translations.literal: Tao held that when the river entered the Luo marshes it would inevitably silt up and grow shallow; he feared Hebei would have no means to resist the enemy, and memorialized: "Before the breach at Xiaowu, though the river shifted repeatedly, it all lay within China, so the capital could take it as the northern boundary.
translations.idiomatic: An Tao argued that if the river were sent into the Luo marshes it would inevitably silt up and shoal, leaving Hebei without a natural barrier against invasion. He memorialized: "Before the Xiaowu breach, the river shifted many times, yet always remained within our territory, so the capital could rely on it as the northern limit.

sentences.zh: 今決而西，則河尾益北，如此不已，將南岸遂屬敵界。

translations.literal: Now broken through to the west, the river's lower course grows ever more northern; if this continues without end, the south bank will become enemy territory.
translations.idiomatic: Now that it has broken westward, the river's lower reach keeps drifting north; if this goes on, the south bank will eventually lie within enemy territory.

sentences.zh: 彼若建橋梁，守以州郡，窺兵河外，可為寒心。

translations.literal: If they build bridges and garrison with prefectures and districts, watching for troops beyond the river—it is enough to chill the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Should they build bridges, hold the crossings with prefectural garrisons, and probe for weakness beyond the river—the prospect is enough to make one shudder.

sentences.zh: 今水官之議，不過論地形，較功費；

translations.literal: Now the water officials' proposal merely discusses terrain and compares labor and expense;
translations.idiomatic: The hydraulic engineers debate only topography and the cost of labor;

sentences.zh: 而獻納之臣，不考利害輕重，徒便於治河，而以設險為緩，非至計也。

translations.literal: yet the ministers who offer advice do not weigh advantage and harm, lightly favoring river control while treating the establishment of strategic barriers as secondary—not the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: and the courtiers who urge adoption never weigh the larger stakes. They fixate on ease of river management and treat strategic defense as an afterthought—that is no sound policy.

sentences.zh: 」帝雖然之，而回河之議紛起，東北蕭然煩費，功亦不就。

translations.literal: " The emperor though approving, yet proposals to redirect the river arose in multitude; the northeast was bleakly burdened with expense, and the project was never accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed in principle, but debate over diverting the river raged on; the northeast was drained by the effort, and in the end the work was never completed.

sentences.zh: 三年，同列皆序遷，且新用執政，燾獨如初。

translations.literal: In the third year, colleagues all promoted in order, and new chief administrators were appointed; Tao alone remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanyou his colleagues were all promoted in turn and new men took the highest offices, yet An Tao alone received no advancement.

sentences.zh: 詔增其兩秩，燾懇辭曰：「是雖有故事，竊意以一時同列超升之故，特用是以慰安其心爾。

translations.literal: An edict increased his two ranks; Tao earnestly declined: "Though there is precedent, I privately think that because colleagues were at one time promoted beyond their turn, this was specially used to comfort their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict came to raise him two ranks in rank. An Tao earnestly declined: "There is precedent for such a grant, but I suspect it was devised only to console colleagues who had been passed over when others were promoted ahead of them.

sentences.zh: 今日願自臣革之，使朝廷不為姑息，而大臣稍敦廉恥之風，庶或有補。

translations.literal: Today I wish to reform this starting from myself, so the court does not indulge, and great ministers somewhat cultivate the wind of integrity and shame—perhaps there may be some benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Let me be the one to break that custom, so the court ceases to indulge favoritism and senior officials recover some sense of honor and shame—it may do a little good.

sentences.zh: 」竟不受。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the promotion to the end.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去，卒喪，拜觀文殿學士、知鄭州，徙潁昌及河南府，入為門下侍郎。

translations.literal: He left on account of mourning for his mother; when mourning ended, he was appointed Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Zhengzhou, transferred to Yingchang and Henan Prefecture, and entered court as vice director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother. When the mourning period ended he was made Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Zhengzhou, then transferred to Yingchang and Henan Prefecture, and finally recalled as vice director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 宣仁之喪，宗室既為三年服，才越歲，章惇拜相，欲革為期。

translations.literal: At Xuanren's funeral the imperial clan had already observed three-year mourning; barely a year had passed when Zhang Dun became chief councillor and wished to change it to one-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At Empress Dowager Xuanren's funeral the imperial clan had already begun three-year mourning; scarcely a year later Zhang Dun became chief councillor and sought to shorten it to one year.

sentences.zh: 燾爭之曰：「上以先后保佑之久，追崇如恐不盡，茲用明道故實耳。

translations.literal: Tao contested: "Above, because of the late empress's long protection, in posthumous honors they fear not doing enough—therefore these Mingdao precedents are used.
translations.idiomatic: An Tao objected: "The throne granted such honors because the late empress had guarded the dynasty for so long—fearing that no tribute could be enough. The Mingdao precedents were chosen for that reason.

sentences.zh: 遽改之，播諸天下，非佳聲也。

translations.literal: To change it hastily and broadcast it to all under heaven—is not a good reputation.
translations.idiomatic: To alter that now and proclaim the change to the empire would not reflect well on the court.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " And so it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The change was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 燾與惇布衣交，覬其助己，燾不肯少下之。

translations.literal: Tao and Dun had been friends as commoners; Dun hoped Tao would help him; Tao would not defer to him in the slightest.
translations.idiomatic: An Tao and Zhang Dun had been friends since their days as commoners. Zhang Dun expected An Tao's support; An Tao would not yield to him in the least.

sentences.zh: 陽翟民蓋漸有財訟，而與諫官來之邵交通，開封得其事。

translations.literal: A man of Yangdi named Gai Jian had a property lawsuit and had dealings with remonstrance official Lai Zhishao; Kaifeng Prefecture got hold of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: A Yangdi resident named Gai Jian was embroiled in a property dispute and had improper contact with the remonstrance official Lai Zhishao; Kaifeng Prefecture uncovered the affair.

sentences.zh: 惇右之邵，欲薄其罪，燾不可；

translations.literal: Dun sided with Zhishao and wished to lighten his offense; Tao would not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun took Lai Zhishao's side and tried to minimize his guilt; An Tao would not agree;

sentences.zh: 復欲並劾開封，燾又不可，遂與惇隙。

translations.literal: he again wished to impeach Kaifeng together; Tao again would not permit; thus he and Dun became estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun then tried to impeach Kaifeng Prefecture as well; An Tao again refused—and the two men broke with each other.

sentences.zh: 明堂齋祠，為儀仗使，後官有絕馳道穿仗而過者，燾方舉劾，諫官常安民又言，教坊不當於相國寺作樂。

translations.literal: At the Hall of Brightness fasting sacrifices, serving as ceremonial guard commissioner, women of the inner quarters cut across the imperial roadway through the guard formation; Tao was just about to impeach when remonstrance official Chang Anmin also spoke: the Music Bureau ought not perform at Xiangguo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hall of Brightness fasting rites, where he served as ceremonial guard commissioner, palace women cut straight across the imperial processional way through the guard lines. An Tao was preparing to impeach them when the remonstrance official Chang Anmin also protested that the Music Bureau should not perform at Xiangguo Temple.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，欲逐安民，燾為救釋。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and wished to banish Anmin; Tao interceded to secure his release.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and wanted to banish Chang Anmin; An Tao intervened and secured his pardon.

sentences.zh: 惇遂譖其相表裏，出知鄭州，徙大名。

translations.literal: Dun then slandered them as acting in concert inside and out; Tao was sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou, then transferred to Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun then accused them of colluding inside and outside the court. An Tao was sent out to serve as prefect of Zhengzhou, then transferred to Daming.

sentences.zh: 父日華，本三班院吏，以燾恩封光祿大夫，至是卒，年九十餘，燾免喪。

translations.literal: His father Rihua had originally been a clerk in the Three-Rank Courtyard; through Tao's grace he was enfeoffed as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; at this time he died at over ninety; Tao completed mourning.
translations.idiomatic: His father An Rihua had begun as a clerk in the Three-Rank Courtyard and, through his son's favor, had been ennobled as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness. He now died at more than ninety; An Tao completed the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，復知樞密院。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended, Tao again became director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong took the throne, An Tao was again appointed director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 舊制，內侍出使，以所得旨言於院，審實乃得行。

translations.literal: By old regulation, when eunuchs went on missions they reported the orders received to the bureau; only after verification could they proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules, when palace eunuchs were dispatched on missions they had to report the orders they had received to the bureau and could not act until the instructions were verified.

sentences.zh: 後多輒去，燾請按治之。

translations.literal: Later many would leave straightaway; Tao requested investigation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In time many simply departed without doing so; An Tao asked that they be investigated and punished.

sentences.zh: 都知閻守懃領他職，祈罷不以告，亦劾之，帝敕守懃詣燾謝。

translations.literal: Chief eunuch Yan Shougong held another post and prayed to be relieved without reporting it; Tao also impeached him; the emperor ordered Shougong to go to Tao to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The chief eunuch Yan Shougong had taken another appointment and petitioned for release without informing the bureau; An Tao impeached him as well, and the emperor ordered Yan Shougong to go to An Tao and apologize.

sentences.zh: 郝隨得罪，或揣上意且起用，欲援赦為階，亦爭之。

translations.literal: Hao Sui had been punished; some gauged the emperor's intent that he would soon be reappointed and wished to use the amnesty as a stepping-stone; Tao also contested this.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Sui had fallen from favor; some, reading the emperor's mind, expected his imminent recall and sought to use the general amnesty as a pretext for reinstatement. An Tao opposed that too.

sentences.zh: 以老避位，帝將寵以觀文殿大學士，有間之者曰：「是宰相恩典也。

translations.literal: Retiring due to age, the emperor was about to honor him with Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature; someone who drove a wedge said: "That is a chief councillor's grace.
translations.idiomatic: As he stepped aside on account of age, the emperor meant to honor him with the title Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature. A detractor whispered, "That is a boon reserved for chief councillors.

sentences.zh: 」但以學士知河南。

translations.literal: " He was only made academician and prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He received only the lower rank of academician and was made prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 將行，上疏曰：「自紹聖、元符以來，用事之臣，持紹述之名，誑惑君父，上則固寵位而快恩仇，下則希進用而肆朋附。

translations.literal: About to depart, he submitted a memorial: "Since Shaosheng and Yuanfu, the ministers in power, wielding the name of 'succession,' deceived ruler and father—above to secure favored positions and satisfy grudges, below to hope for advancement and indulge factional attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving the capital he submitted a memorial: "Since the Shaosheng and Yuanfu reigns, the men who have held power under the banner of 'continuing the legacy' have misled their sovereign—above, to cling to favor and settle old scores; below, to win promotion and indulge faction.

sentences.zh: 彼自為謀則善矣，未嚐有毫髮為公家計者也。

translations.literal: They plan well for themselves, yet never contributed even a hair's breadth for the public good.
translations.idiomatic: They schemed ably for themselves, but never spared so much as a thought for the public weal.

sentences.zh: 夫聽言之道，必以其事觀之。

translations.literal: The way of listening to words must be to observe through the deeds.
translations.idiomatic: The proper way to weigh words is to judge them by their results.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢高談遠引，獨以神考之事切於今者為證。

translations.literal: I dare not discourse loftily and cite distant examples; I take only matters of the late Shenzong that bear directly on the present as proof.
translations.idiomatic: I will not indulge in lofty rhetoric or distant precedents; I cite only what touches the present from the reign of the late Emperor Shenzong.

sentences.zh: 熙寧、元豐之間，中外府庫，無不充衍，小邑所積錢米，亦不減二十萬，紹聖以還，傾竭以供邊費，使軍無見糧，吏無月俸，公私虛耗，未有甚於此時，而反謂紹述，豈不為厚誣哉！

translations.literal: Between Xining and Yuanfeng, treasuries within and without were all abundantly filled; even small districts accumulated no less than two hundred thousand in cash and grain; since Shaosheng, everything has been drained to supply frontier costs, leaving troops without provisions in hand, officials without monthly salaries—public and private wastage has never been worse than now, yet they call it 'succession'—is this not a gross deception!
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xining and Yuanfeng reigns, treasuries at every level overflowed; even small counties held no less than two hundred thousand in cash and grain. Since Shaosheng the state has been bled dry to pay for the frontier, until soldiers have no rations in hand and officials no monthly pay. Never has waste been so severe—yet they call this 'continuing the legacy.' What gross deception is this!

sentences.zh: 願陛下監之，勿使飾偏辭而為身謀者復得行其說。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to take heed, and not let those who dress up partial words to scheme for themselves again have their doctrines implemented.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to take warning, and not allow those who cloak self-interest in one-sided arguments to prevail again.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「東京黨禍已萌，願戒履霜之漸。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The Eastern Capital faction disaster has already sprouted; I pray Your Majesty guard against the gradual progress of treading on frost.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Faction strife at the Eastern Capital has already begun; Your Majesty should heed the warning that great troubles start from small signs."

sentences.zh: 」語尤激切。

translations.literal: " His words were especially impassioned and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: His language was especially forceful and urgent.

sentences.zh: 初，建青唐邈川為湟州，戍守困於供億。

translations.literal: Initially, Qingtang Miaochuan was established as Huangzhou; the garrison troops were distressed by provisioning.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingtang Miaochuan was first made into Huangzhou Prefecture, the garrison struggled under the burden of supply.

sentences.zh: 燾在樞府，因議者以為可棄，奏還之。

translations.literal: Tao was at the Privy Council; because discussants held that it could be abandoned, he memorialized to have it returned.
translations.idiomatic: An Tao, then serving at the Privy Council, joined those who argued the post should be abandoned and memorialized for its withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年議其罪，降端明殿學士，再貶寧國軍節度副使，漢陽軍安置。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning his offense was deliberated; he was demoted to Scholar of the Hall of Enlightened Governance, then further demoted to Vice Commissioner of the Ningguo Army and assigned to residence at Hanyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 1 (1102), his case was reviewed. He was stripped to Scholar of the Hall of Enlightened Governance, then demoted again to Vice Commissioner of the Ningguo Army and exiled under restraint to Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 湟州復，又降祁州團練副使。

translations.literal: When Huangzhou was recovered, he was again demoted to Vice Regimental Trainer of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Huangzhou was retaken, he was demoted once more to Vice Regimental Trainer at Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 鄯州之復，又移建昌軍，然棄鄯州時，燾居憂不預也，終不敢自明。

translations.literal: When Shanzhou was recovered, he was again transferred to Jianchang Army; yet when Shanzhou was abandoned, Tao was in mourning and did not participate—he never dared to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanzhou was retaken, he was reassigned to Jianchang Army. But he had been in mourning when Shanzhou was given up and had played no part in that decision; to the end he did not dare defend himself.

sentences.zh: 閱再歲，始復通議大夫，還洛卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: After two years had passed, he was at last restored to Grand Master for Glorious Manifestation; he returned to Luoyang and died there, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was restored to Grand Master for Glorious Manifestation. He returned to Luoyang, where he died at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 後五歲，悉還其官職。

translations.literal: Five years later, all his offices were fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Five years after that, all his former ranks were posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 子扶，靖康時為給事中。

translations.literal: His son Fu, during the Jingkang era, served as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu was Supervising Censor at the time of the Jingkang crisis.

sentences.zh: 金人入京師，責取金帛，扶與梅執禮、陳知質、程振皆見殺。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens entered the capital and demanded gold and silk, Fu, together with Mei Zhili, Chen Zhizhi, and Cheng Zhen, were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin entered the capital and demanded gold and silk tribute, Fu was executed together with Mei Zhili, Chen Zhizhi, and Cheng Zhen.

sentences.zh: 張璪，初名琥，字邃明，滁州全椒人，洎之孫也。

translations.literal: Zhang Can, original name Hu, courtesy name Suiming, was a man of Quanjiao in Chuzhou and a grandson of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Can, originally named Hu, courtesy name Suiming, was a native of Quanjiao in Chuzhou and a grandson of Zhang Ji.

sentences.zh: 早孤，鞠於兄環，欲任以官，辭不就。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he was raised by his elder brother Huan, who wished to grant him office; he declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Left fatherless young, he was raised by his elder brother Huan, who sought to place him in office, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 未冠登第，歷鳳翔法曹、縉雲令。

translations.literal: Before reaching majority he passed the examinations; he served as legal clerk at Fengxiang and as magistrate of Jinyun.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations before coming of age and served successively as judicial clerk at Fengxiang and magistrate of Jinyun.

sentences.zh: 王安石與環善，既得政，將用之，而環已老，乃引璪同編修中書條例，授集賢校理、知諫院、直舍人院。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi was on good terms with Huan; once he obtained power he intended to employ Huan, but Huan was already old, so he brought Can in to jointly compile the Central Secretariat regulations, appointing him Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Remonstrance Officer, and Commissioner of the Drafting Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi, who was close to Huan, planned to appoint him once he took power, but Huan was already elderly. Wang therefore brought Can in to help revise the Central Secretariat regulations and gave him collator's rank in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, the post of remonstrance officer, and duty in the Drafting Academy.

sentences.zh: 楊繪、劉摯論助役，安石使璪為文詰之，辭，曾布請為之，由是忤安石意。

translations.literal: When Yang Hui and Liu Zhi debated the corvée-exemption policy, Anshi had Can write an essay challenging them; Can declined; Zeng Bu asked to do it instead, and by this he offended Anshi's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Hui and Liu Zhi criticized the corvée-exemption law, Anshi asked Can to draft a rebuttal; Can refused. Zeng Bu volunteered instead, and Can thereby fell from Anshi's favor.

sentences.zh: 神宗欲命璪知制誥，安石薦用布，以璪同修起居注。

translations.literal: Shenzong wished to appoint Can Drafting Academician; Anshi recommended employing Bu and had Can compile the Diary of Activity and Repose instead.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong meant to appoint Can Drafting Academician, but Anshi put Bu in that role and relegated Can to compiling the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 自縣令至是，才歲餘。

translations.literal: From magistrate to these posts was little more than one year.
translations.idiomatic: It had been barely more than a year since he left the county magistracy.

sentences.zh: 坐奏事不實，解三職，已而復之。

translations.literal: He was punished for memorializing on matters that were not true and was relieved of three posts; before long he was restored.
translations.idiomatic: He lost all three offices for an inaccurate memorial but was soon reinstated.

sentences.zh: 時建議武學，璪言：「古之太學，舞干習射，受成獻功，莫不在焉。

translations.literal: At that time a military academy was proposed; Can said: "In antiquity the Grand Academy included drilling with shields and practicing archery, receiving completed learning and presenting achievement—none of these was absent there.
translations.idiomatic: When plans were drawn up for a military academy, Can argued, "The ancient Grand Academy combined shield drill and archery with civil instruction and the ceremonies for presenting students' accomplishments—nothing was left out.

sentences.zh: 文武之才，皆自此出，未聞偏習其一者也。

translations.literal: Talents both civil and military all issued from this; one never heard of training exclusively in only one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military talent alike came from that single school; there was no tradition of cultivating one to the exclusion of the other.

sentences.zh: 請無問文武之士，一養於太學。

translations.literal: I request that without distinction between civil and military scholars, all be nurtured together in the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Let civil and military students alike be educated together in the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷既復河、隴，欲因勢戡定夔、蜀、荊、廣諸夷，璪言：「先王務治中國而已。

translations.literal: " The court had already recovered He and Long and wished to take advantage of momentum to pacify the Yi of Kuizhou, Shu, Jing, and Guang; Can said: "Former kings devoted themselves only to governing China.
translations.idiomatic: After the court retook the He and Long regions, it planned to push on into the tribal territories of Kuizhou, Sichuan, Jing, and Guang. Can said, "The sage kings of old concerned themselves with governing China alone.

sentences.zh: 今生財未盡有道，用財未盡有禮，不宜遽及徂征之事。

translations.literal: Now revenue has not yet been fully produced by the Way, nor expenditure fully governed by ritual propriety; it is not fitting hastily to touch upon distant campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: We have not yet fully realized the Way in producing wealth or in spending it with ritual restraint; this is no time to launch distant campaigns.

sentences.zh: 」皆不聽。

translations.literal: " None of this was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The court ignored all of it.

sentences.zh: 以集賢殿修撰知蔡州，復知諫院兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: As Academician-Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies he became prefect of Caizhou; he was again made remonstrance officer while concurrently serving as chief supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: As Academician-Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies he was appointed prefect of Caizhou and again given charge of the remonstrance bureau and the supervising censorate.

sentences.zh: 盧秉行鹽法於東南，操持峻急，一人抵禁，數家為黥徙，且破產以償告捕，二年中犯者萬人。

translations.literal: Lu Bing enforced the salt monopoly in the southeast with harsh severity: one person's violation led to several households being tattooed and exiled; families were ruined to pay informants and bounty hunters; within two years ten thousand persons were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bing's enforcement of the salt monopoly in the southeast was merciless: a single offense could send whole households into tattooed exile, while ruined families paid informants' bounties; within two years ten thousand people were convicted.

sentences.zh: 璪條列其狀。

translations.literal: Can itemized these conditions in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Can laid out these abuses in detail.

sentences.zh: 又言：「行役法以來，最下戶亦每歲納錢，乞度寬羨數均損之，以惠貧弱。

translations.literal: He also said: "Since the corvée-exemption law was enacted, even the lowest households pay cash every year; I beg that surplus funds be measured and the levy adjusted proportionally to aid the poor and weak.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that, because the corvée-exemption levy now fell even on the poorest households each year, surplus collections be recalculated and the burden equalized to relieve the indigent.

sentences.zh: 」後皆施行。

translations.literal: " Later all were put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Both recommendations were eventually adopted.

sentences.zh: 鄭俠事起，璪媚呂惠卿，劾馮京與俠交通有跡，深其辭，致京等於罪。

translations.literal: When the Zheng Xia affair arose, Can curried favor with Lü Huiqing and impeached Feng Jing for collusion with Xia on evidence of contact; he piled on the language and brought Feng and others to conviction.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zheng Xia affair Can aligned himself with Lü Huiqing, accused Feng Jing of proven contact with Xia, embroidered the charges, and secured convictions against Feng and others.

sentences.zh: 判司農寺，出知河陽。

translations.literal: He served as chief of the Ministry of Revenue's agricultural directorate, then was dispatched to govern Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief of the Ministry of Revenue's agricultural directorate, then sent out as prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，入權度支副使，遂知制誥、知諫院。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanfeng era he entered as acting Vice Commissioner of Revenue and soon became Drafting Academician and remonstrance officer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanfeng he entered court as acting Vice Commissioner of Revenue and soon became Drafting Academician and remonstrance officer.

sentences.zh: 判國子監，薦蔡卞可為直講。

translations.literal: As director of the Directorate of Education he recommended Cai Bian as regular lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: As director of education he recommended Cai Bian for a lectureship.

sentences.zh: 建增博士弟子員，月書、季考，歲校，以行藝次升，略仿《周官》鄉比之法，立齋舍八十二。

translations.literal: He proposed increasing the number of doctoral students and disciples, with monthly reports, seasonal examinations, and annual reviews, advancement by order of conduct and achievement after the manner of the Zhou offices' village comparison system, and established eighty-two dormitory halls.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded the quota of doctoral students, instituted monthly progress reports, quarterly exams, and annual reviews with promotion by character and achievement in rough imitation of the Zhou rite of local comparison, and built eighty-two dormitory halls.

sentences.zh: 學官之盛，近代莫比，其議多自璪發之。

translations.literal: The splendor of the educational offices had no parallel in recent times; most of these proposals originated with Can.
translations.idiomatic: The state academies had never enjoyed such prosperity in living memory, and most of the reforms were Can's doing.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾下臺獄，璪與李定雜治，謀傅致軾於死，卒不克。

translations.literal: When Su Shi was thrown into censorial prison, Can jointly investigated with Li Ding, plotting to manufacture a capital charge against Shi, but in the end did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi was thrown into the Censorate prison, Can joined Li Ding in investigating him and tried to frame him on a capital charge, but failed.

sentences.zh: 詳定郊廟奉祀禮文，議者多以國朝未嘗躬行方澤之禮為非，正詔議更制。

translations.literal: While collating ritual texts for suburban and ancestral sacrifices, many critics objected that the dynasty had never personally performed the Fangze rite; an edict ordered reconsideration and revision.
translations.idiomatic: In revising suburban and ancestral ritual texts, many argued that the dynasty had never performed the Fangze sacrifice in person; the emperor ordered the rites redrafted.

sentences.zh: 璪請於夏至之日，備禮容樂舞，以塚宰攝事。

translations.literal: Can asked that on the summer solstice full ritual, music, and dance be prepared, with the Chief Minister officiating by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: Can proposed restoring the Fangze rite on the summer solstice with full ceremonial, music, and dance, the chief minister standing in for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「在今所宜，無以易此。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For the present this is what is suitable; nothing should replace this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "This is exactly what the times require; there is no better alternative.

sentences.zh: 」卒行其說。

translations.literal: " In the end his proposal was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Can's plan was adopted in the end.

sentences.zh: 為翰林學士，詳定官制，以寄祿二十四階易前日省、寺虛名，而職事名始正。

translations.literal: As Hanlin Academician he collated the official system, replacing the former empty titles of ministries and directorates with twenty-four nominal salary ranks, so that functional titles at last corresponded to real duties.
translations.idiomatic: As Hanlin Academician he helped reform the bureaucracy, substituting twenty-four salary grades for the hollow provincial and directorate titles of earlier days and aligning office names with actual work.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜參知政事，改中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor and promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he received appointment as Vice Grand Councillor with the title Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，諫官、御史合攻之，謂：「璪奸邪便佞，善窺主意，隨勢所在而依附之，往往以危機陷人。

translations.literal: When Zhezong ascended, remonstrance officers and censors jointly attacked him, saying: "Can is treacherous, fawning, and adept at reading the sovereign's mind; wherever the prevailing trend lies he attaches himself, often entrapping others with perilous charges.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhezong's accession, remonstrance officers and censors assailed him together, declaring, "Can is a sycophant who reads the throne's mood, attaches himself to every faction in turn, and routinely traps rivals with dangerous charges.

sentences.zh: 深交舒亶，數起大獄，天下共知其為大奸。

translations.literal: He was deeply allied with Shu Dan and repeatedly launched great prosecutions; the empire together knows him to be a great villain.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Shu Dan and repeatedly stirred up major prosecutions; throughout the realm he was known as an arch-villain.

sentences.zh: 小人而在高位，德之賊也。

translations.literal: A petty man in high office is the thief of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: A villain in high place is the enemy of public morals.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，皆不報。

translations.literal: " When the memorials were submitted, none received response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials went in; none drew a reply.

sentences.zh: 最後，劉摯言：「璪初奉安石，旋附惠卿，隨王珪，黨章惇，諂蔡確，數人之性不同，而能探情變節，左右從順，各得其歡心。

translations.literal: Finally Liu Zhi said: "Can at first attached himself to Anshi, then soon to Huiqing, followed Wang Gui, banded with Zhang Dun, and flattered Cai Que—men of different temper, yet he could probe their feelings, change his conduct, turn this way and that in compliance, and win each man's goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: At last Liu Zhi wrote, "Can first served Anshi, then quickly clung to Huiqing, followed Wang Gui, joined Zhang Dun's faction, and flattered Cai Que—very different men, yet he could read each one, shift his allegiance, and accommodate himself until he won every patron's favor.

sentences.zh: 今過惡既章，不可不速去。

translations.literal: Now that his crimes and wickedness are plain, he must not be allowed to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: His misconduct is now manifest; he should be dismissed without delay.

sentences.zh: 」如是逾歲，乃以資政殿學士知鄭州，徙河南、定州、大名府，進大學士，知揚州以卒。

translations.literal: " Thus after more than a year, he was made Scholar of the Hall of Proclaimed Governance and appointed prefect of Zhengzhou, transferred to Henan, Dingzhou, and Daming Prefecture, promoted to Grand Academician, and died while serving as prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year passed before he was finally removed, appointed Scholar of the Hall of Proclaimed Governance and prefect of Zhengzhou, then transferred through Henan, Dingzhou, and Daming, promoted to Grand Academician, and died in office at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 贈右銀青光祿大夫，諡曰「簡翼」。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Right Silver Lustre Grand Master of the Palace; posthumous epithet "Jianyi."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Silver Lustre Grand Master of the Palace, with the posthumous name Jianyi ("Simple and Steadfast").

sentences.zh: 蒲宗孟

translations.literal: Pu Zongmeng
translations.idiomatic: Pu Zongmeng

sentences.zh: 蒲宗孟，字傳正，閬州新井人。

translations.literal: Pu Zongmeng, courtesy name Chuanzheng, was a man of Xinjing in Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Zongmeng, style name Chuanzheng, was a native of Xinjing in Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調夔州觀察推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed investigating assistant magistrate of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After placing among the jinshi, he was assigned as investigating assistant magistrate in Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 治平中，水災地震，宗孟上書，斥大臣及宮禁、宦寺，熙寧元年，改著作佐郎。

translations.literal: During the Zhiping era, when floods and earthquakes struck, Zongmeng submitted a memorial denouncing chief ministers as well as the palace precinct and the eunuch establishment; in the first year of Xining he was transferred to Assistant Editorial Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhiping period, after floods and earthquakes, Zongmeng memorialized the throne, attacking senior ministers along with the inner palace and the eunuch bureaucracy. In the first year of Xining he was made Assistant Editorial Director.

sentences.zh: 神宗見其名，曰：「是嘗言水災地震者邪？

translations.literal: When Shenzong saw his name, he said: "Is this the man who once spoke about floods and earthquakes?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong saw his name, he asked, "Isn't this the man who once warned about floods and earthquakes?

sentences.zh: 」召試學士院，以為館閣校勘、檢正中書戶房兼修條例，進集賢校理。

translations.literal: " He was summoned for examination at the Hanlin Academy, then appointed Collator in the Palace Library, Rectifier in the Central Secretariat Revenue Section with concurrent duty revising regulations, and advanced to Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: " He was called to the Hanlin Academy for examination and appointed collator in the Palace Library, rectifier in the Central Secretariat's Revenue Section with concurrent work on regulatory revisions, and then promoted to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 時三司新置提舉帳司官，祿豐地要，人人欲得之。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Commissions had newly established posts of ledger supervisors; the salary was rich and the position influential, and everyone wanted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Commissions had just created ledger-supervisor posts—lucrative and powerful—and every official wanted one.

sentences.zh: 執政上其員，帝命與宗孟。

translations.literal: The chief councilors submitted a list of candidates, and the emperor assigned the post to Zongmeng.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief ministers submitted their nominees, the emperor gave the appointment to Zongmeng.

sentences.zh: 命察訪荊湖兩路，奏罷辰、沅役錢及湖南丁賦，遠人賴之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to inspect the Jing and Hu circuits, memorialized to abolish corvée levies in Chen and Yuan and the household tax in Hunan, and the people of the remote regions relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned to inspect the Jing and Hu circuits, he memorialized to abolish corvée payments in Chen and Yuan and the household levy in Hunan, to the great relief of people in the frontier districts.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿制手實法，然猶許災傷五分以上不預。

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing devised the hand-real-property law, yet still allowed those with disaster losses of five-tenths or more not to participate.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing drafted the hand-real-property law, but still exempted households that had suffered disaster losses of fifty percent or more.

sentences.zh: 宗孟言：「民以手實上其家之物產而官為注籍，以正百年無用不明之版圖而均齊其力役，天下良法也。

translations.literal: Zongmeng said: "The people report their household property by hand-real declaration and the government registers it, thereby correcting century-old useless and unclear land registers and equalizing corvée burdens—this is an excellent law for the realm.
