translations.idiomatic: Zongmeng argued, "When households declare their property under the hand-real system and the state registers it, century-old land records are finally brought into order and corvée burdens equalized. For the empire this is an excellent law.

sentences.zh: 然災傷五分不預焉。

translations.literal: Yet those with disaster losses of five-tenths do not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet households with disaster losses of fifty percent are still left out.

sentences.zh: 臣以為使民自供，初無所擾，何待豐歲？

translations.literal: Your subject considers that having the people supply the information themselves initially involves no disturbance—why wait for a bountiful year?
translations.idiomatic: I believe self-reporting imposes no real hardship in the first place—why should the law wait for a good harvest year?

sentences.zh: 願詔有司，勿以豐凶弛張其法。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will decree to the responsible offices that they not loosen or tighten the law according to good or bad harvest years.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty instruct the responsible agencies not to relax or tighten the law according to whether the harvest is good or bad.

sentences.zh: 」從之，民於是益病矣。

translations.literal: " The request was approved, and from this the people suffered all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed, and the people were burdened all the more.

sentences.zh: 俄同修起居注、直舍人院、知制誥，帝又稱其有史才，命同修兩朝國史，為翰林學士兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Before long he was also appointed to compile the Diary of Activity and Repose, served in the Drafting Academy, and became Drafting Academician; the emperor again praised his talent for history and ordered him to co-compile the national history of two reigns, appointing him Hanlin Academician and Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also compiling the imperial diary, serving in the Drafting Academy, and appointed Drafting Academician. The emperor again praised his historical talent and ordered him to co-author the national history of two reigns, making him Hanlin Academician and Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 舊制，學士唯服金帶，宗孟入謝，帝曰：「學士職清地近，非他官比，而官儀未寵。

translations.literal: By old regulation academicians wore only the gold belt; when Zongmeng came to give thanks, the emperor said: "The academicians' office is pure in rank and close to the throne—not comparable to other posts—yet their ceremonial honors have not been distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, academicians wore only the gold belt. When Zongmeng came to give thanks, the emperor said, "An academician's post is exalted and close to the throne, unlike ordinary offices, yet the ceremonial honors accorded the rank have been insufficient.

sentences.zh: 」乃加佩魚，遂著為令。

translations.literal: " He then added the fish tally for him, and this was established as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore granted him the fish tally as well, and the practice was written into regulation.

sentences.zh: 樞密都承旨張誠一預書局事，頗肆橫，挾中旨以脅同列。

translations.literal: Zhang Chengyi, Chief Coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, participated in the historiography project and acted quite overbearingly, using secret imperial orders to intimidate his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengyi, chief coordinator at the Bureau of Military Affairs, took part in the history project and behaved with great arrogance, wielding secret imperial instructions to bully his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 宗孟持其語質帝前，皆非是，因叩頭白其奸。

translations.literal: Zongmeng brought his statements before the emperor to confront him; none proved true, and he kowtowed to expose his misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmeng repeated Zhang's claims before the emperor and showed that none held up, then kowtowed to denounce his wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 帝察其不阿，欲大用，拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: The emperor saw that he would not flatter, wished to employ him greatly, and appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that he would not truckle to power, the emperor meant to promote him further and appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗語輔臣，有無人才之歎，宗孟率爾對曰：「人才半為司馬光邪說所壞。

translations.literal: The emperor once spoke to his assisting ministers with a sigh about the lack of talented men, and Zongmeng rashly replied: "Half of our talent has been ruined by Sima Guang's heterodox teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Once, lamenting the shortage of capable men, the emperor spoke to his chief ministers, and Zongmeng blurted out, "Half our talent has been spoiled by Sima Guang's perverse doctrines.

sentences.zh: 」帝不語，直視久之，曰：「蒲宗孟乃不取司馬光邪？

translations.literal: " The emperor said nothing, stared at him for a long while, and said: "Does Pu Zongmeng really think Sima Guang is heterodox?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor fell silent, fixed his gaze on him for a long moment, and said, "So Pu Zongmeng considers Sima Guang heterodox, does he?

sentences.zh: 未論別事，只辭樞密一節，朕自即位以來，唯見此一人；

translations.literal: Setting other matters aside, in the single matter of declining the Bureau of Military Affairs, since my accession I have seen only this one man do it;
translations.idiomatic: Never mind other questions—in refusing the Bureau of Military Affairs alone, since I took the throne I have seen only one man do such a thing;

sentences.zh: 他人，則雖迫之使去，亦不肯矣。

translations.literal: as for the others, even if one forced them to leave, they would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: the rest, even if you drove them out, would not go.

sentences.zh: 」宗孟慚懼，至無以為容。

translations.literal: " Zongmeng was ashamed and fearful, until he could hardly contain himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Zongmeng was mortified and afraid, scarcely able to hold himself together.

sentences.zh: 僅一歲，御史論其荒於酒色及繕治府舍過制，罷知汝州。

translations.literal: After only one year, censors impeached him for indulgence in wine and women and for renovating his official residence beyond regulation, and he was dismissed to serve as prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a year later, censors charged him with dissipation in wine and women and with building his official residence beyond what regulations allowed; he was removed and made prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，加資政殿學士，徙、杭、鄆三州。

translations.literal: After another year he was made Scholar of the Hall of Proclaimed Governance and transferred through Xu, Hang, and Yun prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Scholar of the Hall of Proclaimed Governance and served in succession at Xu, Hang, and Yun prefectures.

sentences.zh: 鄆介梁山濼，素多盜，宗孟痛治之，雖小偷微罪，亦斷其足筋，盜雖為衰止，而所殺亦不可勝計矣。

translations.literal: Yun bordered Liangshan Marsh and had long been troubled by bandits; Zongmeng punished them severely, and even for petty theft and minor offenses he severed the tendons of the feet; although banditry did decline, the number he killed was beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhou bordered Liangshan Marsh and had long been infested with bandits. Zongmeng cracked down ruthlessly: even for petty theft he severed the Achilles tendons. Banditry did subside, but the dead were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 方徙河中，御史以慘酷劾，奪職知虢州。

translations.literal: Just as he was transferred to Hedong, censors impeached him for cruelty and stripped his rank, appointing him prefect of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: As he was being transferred to Hedong, censors impeached him for cruelty; he was demoted and sent to serve as prefect of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，復知河中，還其職。

translations.literal: The next year he was again appointed to Hedong and his former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned to Hedong and regained his former rank.

sentences.zh: 帥永興，移大名。

translations.literal: He commanded Yongxing and was then transferred to Daming.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military commissioner at Yongxing, then moved to Daming.

sentences.zh: 宗孟厭苦易地，頗默默不樂，復求河中。

translations.literal: Zongmeng wearied of being transferred from place to place, grew quite silent and unhappy, and again requested Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Weary of constant transfers, Zongmeng grew withdrawn and discontented and asked to return to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 宗孟趣尚嚴整而性侈汰，藏帑豐，每旦刲羊十、豕十，然燭三百入郡舍。

translations.literal: Zongmeng's tastes ran to severity and order, but his character was extravagant; his treasury was rich, and every morning he slaughtered ten sheep and ten pigs and burned three hundred candles upon entering the prefectural residence.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmeng favored strict formality but lived extravagantly. His stores were ample: each morning he had ten sheep and ten pigs slaughtered, and three hundred candles lit when he entered the prefectural compound.

sentences.zh: 或請損之，慍曰：「君欲使我坐暗室忍饑邪？

translations.literal: When someone asked him to cut back, he said angrily: "Do you want me to sit in a dark room and endure hunger?
translations.idiomatic: When someone suggested he economize, he snapped, "Do you expect me to sit in the dark and go hungry?

sentences.zh: 」常日盥潔，有小洗面、大洗面、小濯足、大濯足、小大澡浴之別。

translations.literal: " On ordinary days his ablutions were divided into small face-washing, large face-washing, small foot-washing, large foot-washing, and small and large bathing.
translations.idiomatic: " His daily grooming had separate categories: small face-washing, large face-washing, small foot-washing, large foot-washing, and small and large bathing.

sentences.zh: 每用婢子數人，一浴至湯五斛。

translations.literal: Each time he used several maidservants, and a single bath consumed up to five hu of water.
translations.idiomatic: Several maids attended each session, and a single bath could use as much as five hu of water.

sentences.zh: 他奉養率稱是。

translations.literal: His other provisions were generally on the same scale.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of his household spending matched this scale.

sentences.zh: 嘗以書抵蘇軾云：「晚年學道有所得。

translations.literal: He once wrote to Su Shi, saying: "In my later years I have studied the Way and gained something from it.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote Su Shi, "In my later years I have cultivated the Way and feel I have gained something.

sentences.zh: 」軾答之曰：「聞所得甚高，然有二事相勸：一曰慈，二曰儉也。

translations.literal: " Su Shi replied: "I hear that what you have gained is very lofty, yet I would advise you in two things: the first is compassion, the second is frugality.
translations.idiomatic: " Su Shi answered, "I hear your attainment is lofty indeed, yet I would counsel you in two matters: first, compassion; second, frugality.

sentences.zh: 」蓋針其失云。

translations.literal: " This was meant to needle his faults.
translations.idiomatic: " It was a pointed rebuke of his failings.

sentences.zh: 黃履，字安中，邵武人。

translations.literal: Huang Lü, courtesy name Anzhong, was a man of Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Lü, style name Anzhong, was a native of Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 少遊太學，舉進士，調南京法曹，又為高密、廣平王二宮教授、館閣校勘，同知禮院。

translations.literal: In youth he studied at the Imperial Academy, passed the jinshi examination, and was appointed legal clerk at the Southern Capital; he also served as tutor to the Princes of Gaomi and Guangping, as collator in the Palace Library, and as deputy director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied at the Imperial Academy and passed the jinshi examination. He served as judicial clerk at the Southern Capital, tutor to the Princes of Gaomi and Guangping, collator in the Palace Library, and deputy director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史裏行，辭御史，改崇政殿說書兼知諫院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Acting Investigating Censor, declined the censor's post, and was transferred to Lecturer at the Hall of Exalted Governance with concurrent charge of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to acting investigating censor, he declined the censorate and was made lecturer at the Hall of Exalted Governance while also heading the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 神宗嘗詢天地合祭是非，對曰：「國朝之制，冬至祭天圓丘，夏至祭地方澤，每歲行之，皆合於古。

translations.literal: Shenzong once inquired whether the combined sacrifice of Heaven and Earth was right or wrong, and he replied: "Our dynasty's system sacrifices Heaven at the Round Mound at the winter solstice and Earth at the Square Pond at the summer solstice; performed every year, this accords with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong asked whether the combined sacrifice of Heaven and Earth was correct, Huang Lü answered, "The dynasty sacrifices Heaven at the Round Mound at the winter solstice and Earth at the Square Pond at the summer solstice, each year as the ancients did.

sentences.zh: 猶以有司攝事未足以盡，於是三歲一郊而親行之，所謂因時制宜者也，雖施之方今，為不可易。

translations.literal: Yet because ministers acting as proxies still seemed insufficient to fulfill the rite fully, every three years the emperor personally performs the suburban sacrifice—this is what is called adapting institutions to the times—and even applied to the present day it should not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Because having ministers perform the rites by proxy still seemed inadequate, every three years the emperor conducts the suburban sacrifice in person—an adaptation to the times that should not be altered even now.

sentences.zh: 惟合祭之非，在所當正。

translations.literal: Only the error of the combined sacrifice is what ought to be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Only the combined sacrifice itself is what must be set right.

sentences.zh: 然今日禮文之失，非獨此也，願敕有司正群祀，為一代損益之制。

translations.literal: Yet the defects in today's ritual texts are not limited to this alone; I hope Your Majesty will command the responsible offices to rectify the full range of state sacrifices and establish a system of additions and subtractions for one generation.
translations.idiomatic: Today's ritual errors go beyond this one point. I ask that Your Majesty order the responsible offices to revise the entire sacrificial code and establish a balanced ritual system for the age.

sentences.zh: 」詔置局詳定，命履董之，北郊之議遂定。

translations.literal: " An edict established a bureau for detailed review and ordered Lü to direct it; the debate over the northern suburban sacrifice was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne ordered a review bureau under Lü's direction, and the northern suburban sacrifice was settled.

sentences.zh: 同修起居注，進知制誥、同修國史。

translations.literal: He also compiled the Diary of Activity and Repose, was promoted to Drafting Academician, and co-compiled the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the imperial diary, was promoted to Drafting Academician, and helped compile the National History.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂去，服除，以禮部尚書召。

translations.literal: When his mother died he left office; after the mourning period he was recalled as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He left office upon his mother's death and, after the mourning period, was recalled as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時閩中患苦鹽法，獻言者眾，神宗謂履自閩來，恃以為決。

translations.literal: At that time Fujian was suffering under the salt monopoly and many offered opinions; Shenzong, considering that Lü came from Fujian, relied on him for a final decision.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian was then groaning under the salt monopoly, and memorials poured in. Shenzong, knowing Lü was a Fujian man, looked to him for the decisive answer.

sentences.zh: 履乃陳法甚便，遂不復革，鄉論鄙之。

translations.literal: Lü declared the law very convenient, and so it was not reformed; opinion in his home region despised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Lü declared the law perfectly workable, and reform was dropped. His neighbors at home despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 履以大臣多因細故罰金，遂言：「賈誼有云：『遇之以禮，則群臣自喜。

translations.literal: Because many chief ministers were fined over minor matters, Lü said: "Jia Yi wrote: 'Treat them with ritual, and the multitude of ministers will rejoice of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Noting that many senior ministers were being fined for trifling offenses, Lü said, "Jia Yi wrote, 'Receive them with courtesy, and the ministers will rejoice of themselves.

sentences.zh: 』群臣且然，況大臣乎？

translations.literal: ' If even ordinary ministers are so, how much more so for chief ministers?
translations.idiomatic: ' If that holds for ordinary ministers, how much more for great ministers?

sentences.zh: 使罪在可議，黜之可也；

translations.literal: If the offense is debatable, dismiss them;
translations.idiomatic: If guilt is doubtful, remove them;

sentences.zh: 可恕，釋之可也，豈可罰以示辱哉！

translations.literal: if it may be pardoned, release them—how can one fine them to display humiliation!
translations.idiomatic: if it can be forgiven, pardon them. How can fines be used merely to humiliate!

sentences.zh: 」時又制侍郎以下不許獨對，履言：「陛下博訪萬務，雖遠外微官，猶令獨對，顧於侍從乃弗得願也。

translations.literal: " At that time there was also a regulation forbidding vice-ministers and below from private audience with the emperor; Lü said: "Your Majesty broadly consults on the myriad affairs of state; even distant and minor officials are allowed private audience—yet attendants-in-waiting are denied it.
translations.idiomatic: " A rule then barred vice-ministers and lower ranks from private audience. Lü protested, "Your Majesty seeks counsel on every matter under heaven; even humble officials from afar may speak with you privately—yet your close attendants may not.

sentences.zh: 」遂刊其制。

translations.literal: " The regulation was thereupon revised.
translations.idiomatic: " The rule was amended.

sentences.zh: 御史翟思言事，有旨詰所自來。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Zhai Si spoke on a matter, and an edict demanded to know where his information came from.
translations.idiomatic: When Investigating Censor Zhai Si memorialized on a matter, the throne ordered him to reveal his source.

sentences.zh: 履諫曰：「御史以言為職，非有所聞，則無以言。

translations.literal: Lü remonstrated: "The censor's office consists in speaking; if he has heard nothing, he has nothing to say.
translations.idiomatic: Lü remonstrated, "A censor lives by speaking out. Without something he has heard, he has nothing to report.

sentences.zh: 今乃究其自來，則人將懲之，臺諫不復有聞矣，恐失開言路之意。

translations.literal: Now to investigate where his information came from will make people restrain themselves; the remonstrance and censorial offices will no longer hear anything, and I fear the purpose of opening the avenue of speech will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: If you trace every report to its source, men will hold back; the censorate and remonstrance bureau will fall silent, and the avenue of frank speech will be lost.

sentences.zh: 」事乃寢。

translations.literal: " The matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The inquiry was dropped.

sentences.zh: 先是，北郊之論雖定，猶不果行，履又建言：「陽復陰消，各因其時。

translations.literal: Earlier, although the debate over the northern suburban sacrifice had been settled, it still had not been carried out; Lü again submitted a proposal: "When yang returns and yin recedes, each follows its season.
translations.idiomatic: Although the northern suburban rite had been decided, it had not yet been implemented. Lü memorialized again: "When yang returns and yin withdraws, each has its season.

sentences.zh: 上圓下方，各順其體。

translations.literal: Heaven is round and Earth is square; each accords with its form.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is round and Earth is square; each sacrifice should follow its nature.

sentences.zh: 是以聖人因天祀天，因地祀地，三代至漢，其儀不易。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages sacrificed to Heaven according to Heaven and to Earth according to Earth; from the Three Dynasties through Han the rites did not change.
translations.idiomatic: The sages sacrificed to Heaven as Heaven and to Earth as Earth; from the Three Dynasties through Han the rites remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 及王莽諂事元后，遂躋地位，同席共牢，歷世襲行，不能全革。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang fawned upon Empress Dowager Yuan, he raised Earth's status, set Heaven and Earth at the same mat and shared the sacrificial victim, and this practice was handed down through generations without being fully reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang, flattering Empress Dowager Yuan, elevated Earth's rank and placed Heaven and Earth on one mat with a shared offering—a practice that persisted for generations without full reform.

sentences.zh: 逮神宗考古揆今，以正大典，嘗有意於茲矣。

translations.literal: When Shenzong examined antiquity and measured the present to rectify the great rites, he once had intent regarding this matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong studied antiquity to set the great rites right for his own age, he had already turned his mind to this question.

sentences.zh: 今承先志，當在陛下及二三執政。

translations.literal: Now, continuing the former emperor's will, the decision rests with Your Majesty and the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: To carry forward that intent now falls to Your Majesty and your leading ministers.

sentences.zh: 」哲宗詢諸朝，章惇以為北郊止可謂之社。

translations.literal: " Zhezong consulted the court, and Zhang Dun held that the northern suburban rite could only be called a she sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhezong asked the court, and Zhang Dun argued that the northern suburban rite could only be termed a she sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 履曰：「天子祭天地。

translations.literal: Lü said: "The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Lü replied, "The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 蓋郊者交於神明之義，所以天地皆稱郊。

translations.literal: For the term jiao means meeting with the spirits; therefore both Heaven and Earth are called jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao means communion with the divine; that is why sacrifices to both Heaven and Earth are called jiao.

sentences.zh: 故《詩序》云『郊祀天地』。

translations.literal: Hence the preface to the Book of Songs says 'the jiao sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the preface to the Book of Songs speaks of 'the jiao sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.'

sentences.zh: 若夫社者，土之神而已，豈有祭大祇亦謂之社乎？

translations.literal: As for she, it is only the spirit of the soil—how could sacrificing to the great Earth also be called she?
translations.idiomatic: She, by contrast, is the god of the soil alone. How could a sacrifice to great Earth itself be called she?

sentences.zh: 」哲宗可之，遂定郊議。

translations.literal: " Zhezong approved this, and the suburban debate was settled.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhezong agreed, and the suburban rite was finally settled.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會正言鄒浩以言事貶新州，履曰：「浩以親被拔擢之故，敢犯顏納忠，陛下遽斥之死地，人臣將視以為戒，誰復敢為陛下論得失乎？

translations.literal: When Remonstrance Officer Zou Hao was demoted to Xin Prefecture for speaking out, Lü said: "Because Hao was personally raised and promoted, he dared to speak loyal words to Your Majesty's face; yet Your Majesty suddenly sent him to a place of death—ministers will take this as a warning, and who will again dare speak of gain and loss to Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: When Remonstrance Officer Zou Hao was banished to Xin Prefecture for his memorial, Lü said, "Hao, whom Your Majesty had personally raised, dared speak blunt truth to your face; yet you cast him into exile as good as death. Officials will take warning—who will dare discuss your policies again?

sentences.zh: 乞徙善地。

translations.literal: I beg that he be moved to a less harsh place.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be transferred to a milder post.

sentences.zh: 」坐罷知亳州。

translations.literal: " For this he was punished and dismissed to serve as prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: " For this he was removed and made prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，召為資政殿學士兼侍讀，復拜右丞。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended the throne, Lü was recalled as Scholar of the Hall of Proclaimed Governance and Reader-in-Waiting, and again appointed Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong took the throne, Lü was recalled as Scholar of the Hall of Proclaimed Governance and Reader-in-Waiting and again made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 未逾年，求去，加大學士、提舉中太一宮，卒。

translations.literal: Before a year had passed he requested leave, was made Grand Academician and Supervisor of the Palace of Central Grand Unity, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he asked to retire, was made Grand Academician and supervisor of the Palace of Central Grand Unity, and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：哲宗親政之初，見慮未定，范、呂諸賢在廷，左右弼謨，俾日邇忠讜，疏絕回遹，以端其志向，元祐之治業，庶可守也。

translations.literal: The commentators say: At the beginning of Zhezong's personal rule, his deliberations were unsettled; Fan, Lü, and other worthies were at court, assisting and advising on his left and right, drawing him day by day nearer to loyal remonstrance and keeping flatterers at a distance, so that his orientation might be set straight—the achievements of the Yuanyou governance might thus have been preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators write: When Zhezong first took personal rule, his mind was still unsettled. With Fan, Lü, and other worthy ministers at court to guide him, he might daily have drawn closer to honest counsel and kept sycophants at bay, fixing his course so that the gains of the Yuanyou era could have been preserved.

sentences.zh: 清臣怙才躁進，陰覬柄用，首發紹述之說，以隙國是，群奸洞之，衝決莫障，重為薦紳之禍焉。

translations.literal: Li Qingchen, relying on his talent and rushing forward, secretly coveted power; he was the first to advance the doctrine of restoring ancestral practice, using it to split the national policy; the pack of villains saw the opening, burst through without obstruction, and again brought calamity upon the scholar-official class.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qingchen, arrogant in his talent and hungry for advancement, secretly coveted real power. He first preached the "restore the ancestral way" doctrine, splitting the court over national policy. Once the villains saw the breach, nothing could hold them back, and the scholar-official class suffered anew.

sentences.zh: 至於興大獄以傾馮京、蘇軾者，璪也；

translations.literal: As for raising great prosecutions to overturn Feng Jing and Su Shi—that was Can;
translations.idiomatic: Raising great prosecutions to ruin Feng Jing and Su Shi—that was Zhang Can;

sentences.zh: 助成手實之法，以壞人材、讕司馬光者，宗孟也；

translations.literal: helping to complete the hand-real-property law to ruin talent and slander Sima Guang—that was Zongmeng;
translations.idiomatic: helping perfect the hand-real-property law to ruin talent and defame Sima Guang—that was Pu Zongmeng;

sentences.zh: 訐垂簾之事，擊呂大防、劉摯等去之者，履也。

translations.literal: denouncing the matter of the regency curtain and striking down Lü Dafang, Liu Zhi, and others to remove them—that was Lü.
translations.idiomatic: denouncing the regency and driving out Lü Dafang, Liu Zhi, and the rest—that was Huang Lü.

sentences.zh: 清臣真小人之靡，三子抑其亞乎。

translations.literal: Qingchen was truly the sort of petty man without principle; the three men were perhaps next below him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen was the basest sort of petty man; the other three were scarcely better.

sentences.zh: 燾論議識趣，有可稱述，雖立朝無附，而依違蔡確、章惇間，無所匡建，非大臣之道也。

translations.literal: Tao's discourse and insight were worth recounting; although in court he stood without attachment, he wavered between Cai Que and Zhang Dun and built nothing to rectify the age—not the way of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's views and judgment deserve mention, yet though he stood apart in court he vacillated between Cai Que and Zhang Dun and built nothing of lasting worth—not the conduct of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 蔡挺，字子政，宋城人。

translations.literal: Cai Ting, courtesy name Zizheng, was a man of Songcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ting, style name Zizheng, was a native of Songcheng.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調虔州推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he was made assistant magistrate of Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，以父希言當官蜀，乞代行，遂授陵州團練推官。

translations.literal: When his term was complete, because his father Xi Yan was due to take office in Shu, he begged to go in his stead and was appointed regiment assistant magistrate of Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, his father Xi Yan was slated for appointment in Shu; Ting asked to go in his place and was made regiment assistant magistrate of Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王堯臣安撫陝西，辟管勾文字。

translations.literal: Wang Yao Chen, pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, recruited him as manager of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yao Chen, pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, took him on as document officer.

sentences.zh: 富弼使遼，奏挺從，至雄州，誓書有所更易，遣挺還白。

translations.literal: When Fu Bi went as envoy to Liao, he memorialized that Ting should accompany him; upon reaching Xiong Prefecture, the covenant text had been altered, and he sent Ting back to report.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Bi went on embassy to Liao, he asked that Ting accompany him. At Xiong Prefecture the treaty text had been changed, and Fu sent Ting back to report.

sentences.zh: 仁宗欲知契丹事，召對便殿，挺時有父喪，聽以衫帽入。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong wished to know about Khitan affairs and summoned him for audience in the side hall; Ting was then in mourning for his father and was permitted to enter wearing shirt and hat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong, wanting intelligence on the Khitan, summoned Ting to the side hall. Ting was in mourning for his father but was allowed to appear in everyday dress.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹宣撫陝西、河東，奏挺通判涇州，徙鄜州。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan, pacification commissioner of Shaanxi and Hedong, memorialized that Ting be made military vice-prefect of Jing Prefecture; he was transferred to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan, pacification commissioner of Shaanxi and Hedong, recommended Ting as military vice-prefect of Jing Prefecture; he was later transferred to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 河北多盜，精擇諸郡守，以挺知博州。

translations.literal: Hebei had many bandits, and the prefects of the various commanderies were carefully chosen; Ting was appointed prefect of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rife in Hebei, and prefects were chosen with care; Ting was appointed prefect of Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 申飭屬縣嚴保伍，得居停奸盜者數人，弛其宿負，補為吏，使之察警，盜每發輒得。

translations.literal: He strictly admonished the subordinate counties to tighten the mutual-responsibility groups, apprehended several people who had harbored bandits, canceled their old debts, appointed them as clerks, and had them keep watch and report; whenever bandits acted, they were caught.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the subordinate counties to tighten the mutual-responsibility system, seized several harborers of bandits, canceled their old debts, and enrolled them as clerks to watch and report. Thereafter bandits were caught as soon as they struck.

sentences.zh: 均博平、聊城二縣稅，歲衍鉅萬，三司下其法於四方，然大抵增賦也。

translations.literal: He equalized the taxes of Boing and Liaocheng counties; each year the yield increased by tens of thousands. The Three Departments Commission issued his method throughout the realm, but in the main it amounted to increased levies.
translations.idiomatic: He equalized tax assessments in Boing and Liaocheng counties, yielding tens of thousands of cash each year. The Three Departments Commission promulgated his method empire-wide, but in effect it raised taxes.

sentences.zh: 為開封府推官、提點府界公事。

translations.literal: He served as judicial officer of Kaifeng Prefecture and commissioner for prefectural boundary affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial officer of Kaifeng Prefecture and commissioner for metropolitan boundary affairs.

sentences.zh: 部修六漯河，用李仲昌議，塞北流，入於六漯。

translations.literal: He supervised repair of the Six Lou Rivers, adopting Li Zhongchang's proposal to block the northern flow and divert it into the Six Lou.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw repairs on the Six Lou Rivers, following Li Zhongchang's plan to dam the northern channel and redirect it into the Six Lou system.

sentences.zh: 一夕復決，兵夫芟楗漂溺不可計。

translations.literal: In a single night the dike burst again; soldiers and laborers were cut down by debris and drowned beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Overnight the dike burst again; soldiers and laborers were swept away and drowned in numbers beyond count.

sentences.zh: 降知滁州，言者以為輕，乃貶秩停官。

translations.literal: He was demoted to prefect of Chuzhou; critics held the penalty too light, so his rank was further reduced and his office suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to prefect of Chuzhou, but critics deemed the punishment too lenient, so his rank was cut further and his appointment suspended.

sentences.zh: 越數歲，稍起知南安軍，提點江西刑獄，提舉虔州鹽。

translations.literal: After several years he was gradually restored as military prefect of Nan'an, commissioner of Jiangxi judicial affairs, and commissioner of salt in Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was gradually restored to office as military prefect of Nan'an, judicial commissioner for Jiangxi, and salt commissioner for Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 自大庾嶺下南至廣，驛路荒遠，室廬稀疏，往來無所芘。

translations.literal: From the foot of Dayu Ridge southward to Guang, the courier road was desolate and remote, dwellings sparse, and travelers had nowhere to take shelter.
translations.idiomatic: From the foot of Dayu Ridge south to Guang, the post road was bleak and remote, houses few and far between, and travelers had no shelter along the way.

sentences.zh: 挺兄抗時為廣東轉運使，乃相與謀，課民植松夾道，以休行者。

translations.literal: Ting's elder brother Kang was then transport commissioner of Guangdong; together they devised a plan to levy the people to plant pines along the road to give rest to travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's elder brother Kang was then transport commissioner of Guangdong; the two of them devised a plan to require the people to plant pines along both sides of the road so travelers could rest in the shade.

sentences.zh: 江閩鹽賊率千百為州縣害，挺諭所部與期，使首納器甲，原其罪，得兵械萬計。

translations.literal: Salt smugglers in Jiang and Min gathered by the hundreds and thousands to plague the prefectures and counties. Ting instructed his jurisdiction to set a deadline: whoever surrendered weapons first would be pardoned, and more than ten thousand arms were collected.
translations.idiomatic: Salt smugglers in Jiang and Fujian banded together by the hundreds and thousands to plague the prefectures and counties. Ting ordered his jurisdiction to set a deadline: those who surrendered weapons first would be pardoned, and more than ten thousand arms were turned in.

sentences.zh: 官鹽惡而價貴，盜鹽善而價且下，故私販日滋。

translations.literal: Government salt was inferior yet costly, while smuggled salt was good and its price was falling, so illicit trafficking daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Official salt was poor in quality yet expensive, while smuggled salt was better and its price kept falling, so private trafficking grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 挺簡僚吏至淮轉新鹽，明殿賞，以官數之餘畀之，於是賊黨破散，宿弊遂絕，歲增賣鹽四十萬。

translations.literal: Ting selected officials to go to the Huai region to procure fresh salt, clearly announced rewards and bonuses, and gave them the surplus above official quotas. Thereupon the smuggling bands broke up, long-standing abuses ceased, and annual salt sales rose by four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ting dispatched officials to the Huai region to bring in fresh salt, openly promised rewards, and let them keep whatever exceeded the official quota. The smuggling gangs then broke apart, long-standing abuses ended, and annual salt sales rose by four hundred thousand units.

sentences.zh: 改陝西轉運副使，進直龍圖閣、知慶州，因上書論攻守大計。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice transport commissioner of Shaanxi, promoted to direct associate of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Qingzhou, and submitted a memorial on the grand strategy of attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice transport commissioner of Shaanxi, promoted to direct associate of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Qingzhou, and submitted a memorial setting out the grand strategy of attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 夏人大入，挺盡斂邊戶入保，戒諸砦無出戰。

translations.literal: When the Western Xia invaded in force, Ting gathered all border households into fortified stockades and ordered the forts not to sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tanguts invaded in force, Ting gathered every border household into fortified stockades and ordered the forts not to engage outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 諒祚親帥軍數萬攻大順，挺料城堅不可破，而柔遠城惡，亟遣總管張玉將銳師守之。

translations.literal: Liangzuo personally led tens of thousands to attack Dashun. Ting judged that city's walls too strong to breach, but Rouyuan was weak, so he urgently dispatched commander Zhang Yu with elite troops to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzuo personally led tens of thousands of troops against Dashun. Ting reckoned that city's walls too strong to take, but Rouyuan was poorly fortified, so he urgently sent commander Zhang Yu with crack troops to hold it.

sentences.zh: 先布鐵蒺藜大順城旁水中，騎渡水多躓，驚言有神。

translations.literal: First he laid iron caltrops in the water beside Dashun; cavalry crossing the water often stumbled, and they cried out in alarm that spirits were at work.
translations.idiomatic: He first scattered iron caltrops in the water beside Dashun; cavalry crossing the stream kept stumbling, and in alarm they cried that spirits were at work.

sentences.zh: 過三日不克，諒祚督帳下決戰，挺伏強弩壕外，飛矢貫其鎧，遂引卻。

translations.literal: After three days without success, Liangzuo drove his personal followers to a decisive battle. Ting had strong crossbows ambushed outside the moat; a flying bolt pierced his armor, and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After three days without success, Liangzuo drove his personal guard to a decisive assault. Ting had strong crossbows hidden beyond the moat; a bolt pierced his armor, and he pulled back.

sentences.zh: 移寇柔遠，玉夜斫營，夏人驚擾潰去。

translations.literal: They shifted the attack to Rouyuan; Yu raided their camp at night, and the Xia troops fled in panic and disarray.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy turned on Rouyuan; Zhang Yu raided their camp by night, and the Tangut army broke in panic and fled.

sentences.zh: 環州熟羌思順舉族投諒祚，倚為鄉導。

translations.literal: Sishun, a naturalized Qiang of Huanzhou, led his entire clan to defect to Liangzuo and served as his local guide.
translations.idiomatic: Sishun, a naturalized Qiang chieftain of Huanzhou, brought his whole clan over to Liangzuo and served as his local guide.

sentences.zh: 挺宣言思順且復來，命葺其舊舍，出兵西為迎候之舉。

translations.literal: Ting proclaimed that Sishun would soon return, ordered his old dwelling repaired, and sent troops westward as if to welcome him back.
translations.idiomatic: Ting announced that Sishun was about to return, had his old house restored, and sent troops west as though to welcome him back.

sentences.zh: 諒祚果疑思順，毒之死。

translations.literal: Liangzuo indeed grew suspicious of Sishun and poisoned him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzuo did grow suspicious of Sishun and had him poisoned to death.

sentences.zh: 挺築城馬練平為荔原堡，分屬羌三千人守之。

translations.literal: Ting built a fort at Malianping called Liyuan Bao and assigned three thousand Qiang tribesmen to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Ting fortified Malianping as Liyuan Stockade and posted three thousand Qiang tribesmen to hold it.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，加天章閣待制、知渭州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Ting was made editorial acolyte of the Tianzhang Pavilion and prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong acceded, Ting was made editorial acolyte of the Tianzhang Pavilion and prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 舉籍禁兵悉還府，不使有隱占。

translations.literal: He conducted a full registry of the forbidden troops and returned them all to the prefectural rolls, allowing no concealed holding.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted a full muster of the palace troops and returned every man to the prefectural rolls, tolerating no hidden retention.

sentences.zh: 建勤武堂，五日一訓之，偏伍鉦鼓之法甚備。

translations.literal: He built the Hall of Diligent Military Training and drilled them every five days; the methods of squads with gongs and drums were thoroughly complete.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Hall of Diligent Military Training and drilled the men every five days; the squad formations with gongs and drums were fully systematized.

sentences.zh: 儲勁卒於行間，遇用奇，則別為一隊。

translations.literal: He kept elite soldiers in reserve within the ranks; when special tactics were needed they formed a separate unit.
translations.idiomatic: He held crack troops in reserve within the ranks; when a surprise maneuver was needed, they formed a separate detachment.

sentences.zh: 甲兵整習，常若寇至。

translations.literal: Armor and weapons were kept in order and drilling continued as if enemies were at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Arms and armor were kept in fighting trim, and training went on as though the enemy were always at the gates.

sentences.zh: 又分義勇為伍番，番三千人，參正兵防秋與春，以八月、正月集，四十五日而罷，歲省粟帛、錢緡十三萬有奇。

translations.literal: He also divided the volunteer militia into five rotations of three thousand men each to assist regular troops in autumn and spring defenses; they assembled in the eighth and first months for forty-five days and were disbanded, saving over one hundred thirty thousand in grain, cloth, and coin annually.
translations.idiomatic: He also divided the volunteer militia into five rotations of three thousand men each to support regular troops in the autumn and spring defenses; they assembled in the eighth and first months, served forty-five days, and were dismissed, saving more than one hundred thirty thousand in grain, cloth, and cash each year.

sentences.zh: 括並邊生地冒耕田千八百頃，募人佃種，以益邊儲。

translations.literal: He surveyed and consolidated one thousand eight hundred qing of border lands illegally cultivated, recruited tenants to farm them, and thereby increased frontier reserves.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed and consolidated eighteen hundred qing of illegally cultivated border land, recruited tenants to farm it, and thereby increased frontier stores.

sentences.zh: 取邊民闌市蕃部田八千頃，以給弓箭手。

translations.literal: He took eight thousand qing of lands where border people had encroached on tribal holdings and assigned them to archer-soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He reclaimed eight thousand qing of tribal land that border settlers had seized in illicit market dealings and assigned it to archer-soldiers.

sentences.zh: 又築城定戎軍為熙寧砦，開地二千頃，募卒三千人耕守之。

translations.literal: He also fortified Dingwu Army into the Xining Stockade, opened two thousand qing of land, and recruited three thousand soldiers to farm and guard it.
translations.idiomatic: He also fortified Dingwu Army as Xining Stockade, opened two thousand qing of land, and recruited three thousand soldiers to farm and garrison it.

sentences.zh: 諜告夏人集胡盧河，挺出奇兵迎擊之。

translations.literal: Spies reported the Xia gathering at Hulu River; Ting sent an unexpected force to intercept them.
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported the Tanguts massing at Hulu River; Ting sent a surprise force to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 夏人潰，分諸將躡而討之，蕩其七族。

translations.literal: The Xia collapsed; he sent generals in pursuit and wiped out seven clans.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut force broke; he sent his generals in pursuit and destroyed seven clans.

sentences.zh: 進右諫議大夫，賜金帛三千。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Grand Master and granted three thousand in gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Grand Master and rewarded with three thousand in gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 夏人復犯諸砦，環慶兵不能禦，挺遣張玉以萬人往解其圍。

translations.literal: The Xia again raided the stockades; Huan and Qing troops could not hold them off, so Ting sent Zhang Yu with ten thousand men to relieve the siege.
translations.idiomatic: The Tanguts again struck the stockades; the Huan and Qing garrisons could not hold them, so Ting sent Zhang Yu with ten thousand men to break the siege.

sentences.zh: 慶州軍變，挺討平之，進龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: A mutiny broke out in the Qingzhou army; Ting suppressed it and was made direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: A mutiny erupted in the Qingzhou garrison; Ting put it down and was promoted to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 廣銳卒徙營，眾憚遷，欲為亂，城中震擾，挺推斬首惡十九人，訖徙營。

translations.literal: When Guangrui soldiers were to relocate their camp, the men feared the move and plotted mutiny, throwing the city into turmoil. Ting tried and executed nineteen ringleaders and completed the relocation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guangrui troops were ordered to move camp, the men feared the transfer and plotted mutiny, throwing the city into uproar. Ting tried and executed nineteen ringleaders and saw the relocation through.

sentences.zh: 蕃部歲饑，以田質於弓箭手，過期輒沒。

translations.literal: When tribal peoples starved in bad years they pledged their fields to archer-soldiers; past due, the land was forfeited.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years tribal peoples pawned their fields to archer-soldiers; once the term expired, the land was forfeited.

sentences.zh: 挺為貸官錢，歲息什一，後遂推為蕃漢青苗、助役法。

translations.literal: Ting lent them official funds at ten percent annual interest; this was later extended as the Green Sprouts and corvée-assistance laws for tribes and Han alike.
translations.idiomatic: Ting lent them official funds at ten percent annual interest; the practice was later extended as the Green Sprouts and corvée-assistance programs for tribes and Han settlers alike.

sentences.zh: 又自以意製渡河大索及兵械鐮槍，皆獲其用。

translations.literal: He also designed on his own great ropes for river crossing and military weapons including sickle-spears, all of which proved useful.
translations.idiomatic: He also devised on his own great ropes for river crossings and weapons such as sickle-spears, all of which proved effective in the field.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Xining era he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝問挺涇原訓兵之法，召部將按於崇政殿，善之，下以為諸郡法。

translations.literal: The emperor asked about Ting's methods of drilling troops in Jingyuan Circuit; he summoned Ting's subordinate generals to demonstrate in the Chongzheng Hall, approved them, and issued them as the standard for all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about Ting's methods for drilling troops in Jingyuan Circuit, summoned his subordinate generals to demonstrate in the Chongzheng Hall, approved the system, and promulgated it as the model for all prefectures.

sentences.zh: 河州景思立戰死，帝開天章閣訪執政，挺請行。

translations.literal: When Jing Sil of Hezhou died in battle, the emperor opened the Tianzhang Pavilion to consult the chief ministers; Ting volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Sil of Hezhou fell in battle, the emperor opened the Tianzhang Pavilion to consult his chief ministers; Ting offered to go himself.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此小事，不足煩卿。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is a small matter—not worth troubling you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is a small affair—not worth troubling you with."

sentences.zh: 河朔有警，卿當行矣。

translations.literal: When there is alarm on the Hebei frontier, then you should go.
translations.idiomatic: When there is trouble on the Hebei frontier, that is when you should go."

sentences.zh: 」契丹議雲中地，挺請罷沿邊戍人，示以無事，因乞置三十七將，皆行其策。

translations.literal: The Khitan were negotiating over Yunzhong territory. Ting requested withdrawing border garrisons to show that nothing was amiss, and also asked to establish thirty-seven generals—all his proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan opened talks over Yunzhong territory, Ting proposed withdrawing frontier garrisons to signal that all was calm, and also asked to establish thirty-seven generals; all his recommendations were carried out.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，奏事殿中，疾作而仆，帝親臨賜藥，罷為資政殿學士、判南京留司御史臺。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year, while reporting affairs in the hall he was seized by illness and collapsed. The emperor came in person to give him medicine and removed him as Academic Bachelor of the Hall of Zizheng and judge of the Nanjing Remaining Imperial Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year, while reporting to the throne he was struck by illness and collapsed. The emperor came in person to give him medicine and relieved him of office, appointing him Academic Bachelor of the Hall of Zizheng and judge of the Nanjing Remaining Imperial Censorate.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，薨，年六十六。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng he died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yuanfeng era he died, at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書，諡曰敏肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Minsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Minsu, "Keen and Solemn."

sentences.zh: 挺譎而多知，人莫能窺其城府。

translations.literal: Ting was crafty and full of knowledge; no one could fathom his inner designs.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was cunning and resourceful; no one could read his inner mind.

sentences.zh: 初，為富弼、范仲淹客，頗泄其幾事於呂夷簡以自售。

translations.literal: At first, as a retainer of Fu Bi and Fan Zhongyan, he leaked many of their confidential plans to Lü Yijian to advance himself.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while serving as a retainer to Fu Bi and Fan Zhongyan, he leaked many of their confidential plans to Lü Yijian to advance his own career.

sentences.zh: 在渭久，鬱鬱不自聊，寓意詞曲，有「玉關人老」之歎。

translations.literal: Long stationed at Weizhou, he grew depressed and restless, and poured his feelings into lyrics and songs, sighing over "growing old at Jade Gate Pass."
translations.idiomatic: After long service at Weizhou he grew restless and despondent, and poured his feelings into song lyrics, lamenting that he was "growing old at Jade Gate Pass."

sentences.zh: 中使至，則使優伶歌之，以達於禁掖。

translations.literal: When palace envoys arrived, he had actors sing them so the songs would reach the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: When palace envoys visited, he had actors perform the songs so they would reach the inner court.

sentences.zh: 神宗湣焉，遂有樞密之拜云。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong took pity on him, and thus came his appointment to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong took pity on him, and this is how he came to receive appointment to the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 兄 抗 抗，字子直。

translations.literal: Elder brother: Kang. Kang, style name Zizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother: Kang. Kang, courtesy name Zizhi.

sentences.zh: 中進士，調太平州推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as judicial officer of Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed judicial officer of Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 聞父疾，委官去。

translations.literal: Hearing that his father was ill, he resigned his post and left.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned his father was ill, he resigned his post and went home.

sentences.zh: 稍遷睦親宅講書。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to lecturer at the Hall of Imperial Kinship.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to lecturer at the Hall of Imperial Kinship.

sentences.zh: 英宗在宮邸，器重之，請於安懿王，願得與遊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was still in the princely residence, he held Kang in high regard, asked Prince Anyi for permission, and wished to associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: While still in the princely residence, Emperor Yingzong held Kang in high regard, asked Prince Anyi for permission, and wished to keep his company.

sentences.zh: 每見，必衣冠盡禮，義兼師友。

translations.literal: Whenever they met, he always dressed in full ceremonial garb and treated Kang with complete propriety, honoring him as both teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they met, the prince always dressed in full ceremonial garb and treated Kang with complete propriety, honoring him as both teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 再遷太常博士、通判秦州，為秘閣校理，乞知蘇州。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice prefect of Qinzhou, then made collator of the Secret Archive, and requested appointment as prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice prefect of Qinzhou, then made collator of the Secret Archive, and requested appointment as prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 州並江湖，民田苦風潮害，抗築長堤，自城屬昆山，亙八十里，民得立塍堨，大以為利。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered lakes and rivers; the people's fields suffered from wind and tidal damage. Kang built a long dike from the city wall to Kunshan, spanning eighty li, so the people could raise embankments and levees—a great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture bordered lakes and rivers, and the people's fields suffered from wind and tidal flooding. Kang built a long dike from the city wall to Kunshan, eighty li in length, so farmers could raise embankments and levees—a great benefit to the region.

sentences.zh: 徙廣東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 岑水銅冶廢，官給虛券為市，久不償。

translations.literal: The Censhui copper smeltery had closed; the government issued empty vouchers in payment, and for long they went unredeemed.
translations.idiomatic: The Censhui copper smeltery had shut down; the government paid with worthless vouchers that for years went unredeemed.

sentences.zh: 人無所取資，聚而私鑄，抗盡給之，人得直以止。

translations.literal: People had no means of support and gathered to smelt copper illicitly. Kang paid them all in full, and once they received fair value they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: With no other source of income, people turned to illicit smelting. Kang paid them all in full, and once they received fair value the illegal casting stopped.

sentences.zh: 番禺歲運鹽英、韶，道遠，多侵竊雜惡。

translations.literal: Each year Panyu transported salt to Ying and Shao; the route was long, and much was pilfered or adulterated with inferior goods.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Panyu shipped salt to Yingde and Shaoguan; the route was long, and much was stolen or adulterated along the way.

sentences.zh: 抗命十舸為一運，擇攝官主之，歲終會其殿最，增十五萬緡。

translations.literal: Kang ordered ten boats to form one shipment, chose acting officials to oversee each convoy, and at year's end assessed their performance; revenue increased by one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Kang ordered ten boats to a convoy, chose acting officials to oversee each shipment, and assessed their performance at year's end; revenue rose by one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，召為三司判官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Kang was summoned as judicial official of the Three Departments Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, Kang was summoned to serve as judicial official of the Three Departments Commission.

sentences.zh: 廣部去京師遠，不即至，帝見南來者必問之。

translations.literal: Guangdong was far from the capital and he did not arrive promptly; whenever the emperor saw someone coming from the south he would ask about Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong was far from the capital and Kang did not arrive promptly; whenever the emperor saw anyone coming from the south he would ask after him.

sentences.zh: 及入對，諭曰：「卿乃吾故人，朕望於卿者厚，勿以常禮自疏也。

translations.literal: When he entered for audience, the emperor instructed him: "You are an old acquaintance of mine; my expectations of you are high—do not keep your distance with ordinary formalities."
translations.idiomatic: When he appeared for audience, the emperor told him, "You are an old friend of mine; I expect much of you—do not hold yourself apart with ordinary formalities."

sentences.zh: 」以史館修撰同知諫院。

translations.literal: He was made compiler of the Historiography Institute and associate director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was made compiler of the Historiography Institute and associate director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 方議安懿王典禮，抗引禮為人後之誼，指陳切至，涕淚被面，帝亦感泣。

translations.literal: Just then the court was debating the rites for Prince Anyi. Kang cited the proprieties of becoming an heir, argued pointedly and forcefully, tears streaming down his face; the emperor was moved to weeping as well.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was debating the rites for Prince Anyi, Kang invoked the proprieties of adoption and succession, arguing with force and precision until tears streamed down his face; the emperor wept too.

sentences.zh: 都城大水，抗請見，帝迎問之，抗推原變異，守前說以對。

translations.literal: When the capital was flooded, Kang requested an audience; the emperor came forward to ask him. Kang traced the cause of the calamity and held to his earlier argument in reply.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was flooded, Kang requested an audience; the emperor came forward to question him. Kang traced the cause of the disaster and held to his earlier argument in reply.

sentences.zh: 大臣畏其諫列，白為知制誥，遷龍圖閣直學士、知定州。

translations.literal: The chief ministers feared his remonstrances and had him made drafter of edicts, then transferred as direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers feared his remonstrances and had him made drafter of edicts, then transferred him as direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝惜其去，曰：「第行，且召矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor regretted his departure and said: "Go for now—you will be recalled soon."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regretted losing him and said, "Go for now—you will be recalled soon."

sentences.zh: 郡兵番戍，室家留營多不謹，夫歸輒首原，抗下令悉按以法，戍者感焉。

translations.literal: When prefectural troops rotated to frontier garrison, the families left behind in camp were often careless; when the men returned they always pardoned them first. Kang ordered all offenses prosecuted by law, and the garrison troops were deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: When prefectural troops rotated to frontier duty, the families they left behind in camp were often lax; when the men returned they always pardoned them. Kang ordered every offense prosecuted by law, and the garrison troops were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，趣命為太子詹事，未至而神宗立，改樞密直學士、知秦州。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, Kang was urgently appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; before he arrived, Emperor Shenzong took the throne and he was changed to direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, Kang was urgently appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; before he could take up the post, Emperor Shenzong acceded and he was reassigned as direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 過闕，帝見之，悲慟不自勝，曰：「先帝疾大漸，猶不忘卿。

translations.literal: Passing through the capital, he was received by the emperor, who was overcome with grief and said: "When the late emperor's illness was grave, he still did not forget you."
translations.idiomatic: Passing through the capital, he was received by the emperor, who was overcome with grief and said, "When the late emperor's illness was grave, he still did not forget you."

sentences.zh: 」遂赴鎮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he proceeded to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He then proceeded to his post.

sentences.zh: 秦有質院，質諸羌百餘人，自少至老，扃繫之，非死不出，抗皆縱釋，約毋得擅相仇殺。

translations.literal: Qinzhou had a hostage compound holding more than a hundred Qiang tribesmen from youth to old age, locked up and not released except in death. Kang released them all and bound them by oath not to take private revenge on one another.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou maintained a hostage compound holding more than a hundred Qiang tribesmen from youth to old age, locked away and released only in death. Kang freed them all and bound them by oath not to take private revenge on one another.

sentences.zh: 已而有犯者，斬以徇，莫敢奸令。

translations.literal: When someone later violated the oath, he was beheaded as a public warning, and none dared defy the order.
translations.idiomatic: When someone later broke the oath, he was beheaded as a public warning, and none dared defy the order.

sentences.zh: 居數日，夢英宗召語，眷如平生，欲退復留。

translations.literal: After several days he dreamed that Emperor Yingzong summoned him to speak; the affection was as in life; he wished to withdraw but was kept back.
translations.idiomatic: After several days he dreamed that Emperor Yingzong summoned him to talk; their affection was as in life; he wished to leave but was kept back.

sentences.zh: 覺為家人言，感念歔欷。

translations.literal: Awakening, he told his family and wept with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: When he awoke he told his family and wept with emotion.

sentences.zh: 及靈駕發引之旦，東望號慟，見僚佐於便室，驟得疾卒，年六十。

translations.literal: On the morning the imperial coffin set out, he looked eastward and wailed in grief; meeting his staff in a side room, he was suddenly seized by illness and died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: On the morning the imperial coffin set out, he looked eastward and wailed in grief; meeting his staff in a side room, he was suddenly stricken and died, at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 特贈禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was specially posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 又欲賜諡，吳奎曰：「抗以舊恩，自雜學士贈官，已逾常制。

translations.literal: The court also wished to grant a posthumous title. Wu Kui said: "Because of old favor, Kang has already been posthumously promoted from miscellaneous academician—this already exceeds ordinary precedent."
translations.idiomatic: The court also wished to grant a posthumous title. Wu Kui said, "Out of old favor, Kang has already been posthumously promoted from miscellaneous academician—a step beyond ordinary precedent."

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: The proposal was therefore dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 王韶，字子純，江州德安人。

translations.literal: Wang Shao, style name Zichun, was a man of De'an in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao, courtesy name Zichun, was a native of De'an in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調新安主簿、建昌軍司理參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as registrar of Xin'an and judicial administrator of Jianchang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Xin'an and judicial administrator of Jianchang Army.

sentences.zh: 試制科不中，客遊陝西，訪采邊事。

translations.literal: He failed the special decree examination, traveled as a guest in Shaanxi, and gathered intelligence on frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the special decree examination, traveled in Shaanxi as a guest scholar, and gathered intelligence on frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，詣闕上《平戎策》三篇，其略以為：

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining he came to the capital and submitted three chapters of the "Strategy for Pacifying the Barbarians," the gist of which was:
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xining era he came to court and submitted three chapters of the "Strategy for Pacifying the Barbarians," the gist of which was as follows:

sentences.zh: 「西夏可取。

translations.literal: "The Western Xia can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: "The Western Xia can be taken.

sentences.zh: 欲取西夏，當先復河、湟，則夏人有腹背受敵之憂。

translations.literal: To take the Western Xia, one must first recover the He and Huang regions; then the Xia will face enemies on both front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: To take the Western Xia, we must first recover the He and Huang regions; then the Tanguts will face enemies on both front and rear.

sentences.zh: 夏人比年攻青唐，不能克，萬一克之，必並兵南向，大掠秦、渭之間，牧馬於蘭、會，斷古渭境，盡服南山生羌，西築武勝，遣兵時掠洮、河，則隴、蜀諸郡當盡驚擾，瞎征兄弟其能自保邪？

translations.literal: In recent years the Xia have attacked Qingtang without success; if by chance they should take it, they will surely combine their forces and drive south, plundering heavily between Qin and Wei, pasturing horses at Lan and Hui, cutting off the Gulu frontier, subduing all the raw Qiang south of the mountains, building Wusheng to the west, and sending troops to raid Tao and He from time to time—then the prefectures of Long and Shu will all be thrown into alarm. Can Xiazheng and his brothers protect themselves?
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the Tanguts have attacked Qingtang without success; if they should take it, they will surely combine their forces and drive south, plundering heavily between Qin and Wei, pasturing horses at Lanzhou and Huizhou, cutting off the Gulu frontier, subduing all the raw Qiang south of the mountains, building Wusheng to the west, and sending raiders against Tao and He—then the prefectures of Longxi and Shu will all be thrown into alarm. Can Xiazheng and his brothers protect themselves?

sentences.zh: 今唃氏子孫，唯董氈粗能自立，瞎征、欺巴溫之徒，又法所及，各不過一二百里，其勢豈能與西人抗哉！

translations.literal: Today among the descendants of the Gus, only Dong Zhan can roughly hold his own; Xiazheng, Qibawen, and their kind fall within the Xia's reach, each controlling no more than one or two hundred li—how can their strength resist the Western Xia!
translations.idiomatic: Today among the Gus clan, only Dong Zhan can roughly hold his own; Xiazheng, Qibawen, and their kind fall within Tangut reach, each controlling no more than one or two hundred li—how can their strength resist the Western Xia!

sentences.zh: 武威之南，至於洮、河、蘭、鄯，皆故漢郡縣，所謂湟中、浩、大小榆、枹罕，土地肥美，宜五種者在焉。

translations.literal: South of Wuwei, reaching to Tao, He, Lan, and Shan, all were former Han prefectures and counties—the so-called Huangzhong, Hao, Greater and Lesser Yu, and Baohan—lands fertile and rich, suitable for the five grains, lie there.
translations.idiomatic: South of Wuwei, as far as Tao, He, Lan, and Shan, all were former Han commanderies and counties—the so-called Huangzhong, Hao, Greater and Lesser Yu, and Baohan—where the land is fertile and rich and suited to the five grains.

sentences.zh: 幸今諸羌瓜分，莫相統一，此正可並合而兼撫之時也。

translations.literal: Fortunately the various Qiang are now divided and none holds unified authority—this is precisely the time to combine and win them over together.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately the Qiang tribes are now divided and none holds unified authority—this is precisely the moment to combine and win them over together.

sentences.zh: 諸種既服，唃氏敢不歸？

translations.literal: Once the various tribes submit, would the Gus dare not return?
translations.idiomatic: Once the various tribes submit, would the Gus dare not come over?

sentences.zh: 唃氏歸則河西李氏在吾股掌中矣。

translations.literal: If the Gus return, then the Li clan of Hexi will be in the palm of our hand.
translations.idiomatic: If the Gus come over, the Li clan of Hexi will be in the palm of our hand.

sentences.zh: 且唃氏子孫，瞎征差盛，為諸羌所畏，若招諭之，使居武勝或渭源城，使糾合宗黨，制其部族，習用漢法，異時族類雖盛，不過一延州李士彬、環州慕恩耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, among the Gus' descendants Xiazheng is somewhat strong and is feared by the various Qiang. If we summon and win him over, settle him at Wusheng or Weiyuan city, have him gather his clansmen, control his tribes, and accustom them to Han law, then even if his people grow strong in time they will be no more than a Li Shibin of Yanzhou or a Mu En of Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among the Gus' descendants Xiazheng is relatively strong and feared by the other Qiang. If we summon and win him over, settle him at Wusheng or Weiyuan, have him rally his clansmen, control his tribes, and accustom them to Han law, then even if his people grow strong in time they will be no more than a Li Shibin of Yanzhou or a Mu En of Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 為漢有肘腋之助，且使夏人無所連結，策之上也。」

translations.literal: The Han would gain help at their very elbow, and the Xia would have no allies to link with—this is the highest strategy."
translations.idiomatic: The Song would gain allies at their very side, and the Tanguts would have no one to link up with—this is the best strategy of all."

sentences.zh: 神宗異其言，召問方略，以韶管幹秦鳳經略司機宜文字。

translations.literal: The emperor was struck by his words, summoned him to discuss strategy, and appointed Shao as staff officer for planning in the Qinfeng Circuit Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by his words, summoned him to discuss strategy, and appointed Shao staff officer for planning in the Qinfeng Circuit Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 蕃部俞龍珂在青唐最大，渭源羌與夏人皆欲羈屬之，諸將議先致討。

translations.literal: Among the tribes, Yu Longke at Qingtang was the greatest; the Weiyuan Qiang and the Western Xia both wished to bring him under their control, and the generals debated attacking him first.
translations.idiomatic: Among the tribes, Yu Longke at Qingtang was the most powerful; the Weiyuan Qiang and the Tanguts both sought to bring him under their sway, and the generals debated attacking him first.

sentences.zh: 韶因按邊，引數騎直抵其帳，諭其成敗，遂留宿。

translations.literal: Shao took advantage of an inspection tour of the frontier, led a few horsemen straight to Longke's tent, explained the prospects of success and failure, and stayed the night.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the frontier, Shao led a few horsemen straight to Longke's tent, explained the prospects of victory and defeat, and stayed the night.

sentences.zh: 明旦，兩種皆遣其豪隨以東。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, both tribes sent their chieftains to follow him eastward.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day, both tribes sent their chieftains to follow him east.

sentences.zh: 久之，龍珂率屬十二萬口內附，所謂包順者也。

translations.literal: Before long, Longke led his followers—one hundred twenty thousand people—to submit inward; this was the so-called Baoshun tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Longke led one hundred twenty thousand followers to submit to the court—the so-called Baoshun tribe.

sentences.zh: 韶又言：「渭源至秦州，良田不耕者萬頃，願置市易司，頗籠商賈之利，取其贏以治田。

translations.literal: Shao further said: "From Weiyuan to Qinzhou there are ten thousand qing of good land lying uncultivated. I wish to establish a market-control office to capture merchants' profits and use the surplus to develop the fields."
translations.idiomatic: Shao further said, "From Weiyuan to Qinzhou there are ten thousand qing of good land lying uncultivated. I wish to establish a market-control office to capture merchants' profits and use the surplus to develop the fields."

sentences.zh: 」帝從其言，改著作佐郎，仍命韶提舉。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his proposal, changed his title to Assistant Editorial Director, and still ordered Shao to supervise the project.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his proposal, promoted him to Assistant Editorial Director, and ordered Shao to supervise the project.

sentences.zh: 經略使李師中言：「韶乃欲指占極邊弓箭手地耳，又將移市易司於古渭，恐秦州自此益多事，所得不補所亡。

translations.literal: Circuit commissioner Li Shizhong said: "Shao merely wishes to seize the archer-soldiers' lands on the extreme frontier, and will also move the market-control office to ancient Weizhou. I fear Qinzhou will from this have ever more trouble—the gains will not make up for the losses."
translations.idiomatic: Circuit commissioner Li Shizhong said, "Shao merely wishes to seize archer-soldiers' lands on the extreme frontier and will move the market-control office to ancient Weizhou. I fear Qinzhou will only grow more troubled—the gains will not make up for the losses."

sentences.zh: 」王安石主韶議，為罷師中，以竇舜卿代，且遣李若愚按實。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi supported Shao's proposal, had Shizhong removed, replaced him with Dou Shunqing, and also sent Li Ruoyu to investigate the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi supported Shao's proposal, had Shizhong removed and replaced with Dou Shunqing, and sent Li Ruoyu to investigate.

sentences.zh: 若愚至，問田所在，韶不能對。

translations.literal: When Ruoyu arrived and asked where the land was, Shao could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruoyu arrived and asked where the land was, Shao could not answer.

sentences.zh: 舜卿檢索，僅得地一頃，既地主有訟，又歸之矣。

translations.literal: Shunqing searched and found only one qing of land; since the landowner had a lawsuit pending, it was returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shunqing searched and found only one qing of land; since the landowner had a lawsuit pending, it was returned.

sentences.zh: 若愚奏其欺，安石又為罷舜卿而命韓縝。

translations.literal: Ruoyu memorialized that Shao had deceived them; Anshi again had Shunqing removed and appointed Han Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoyu memorialized that Shao had deceived them; Anshi again had Shunqing removed and appointed Han Zhen.

sentences.zh: 縝遂附會實其事，師中、舜卿皆坐謫，而韶為太子中允、秘閣校理。

translations.literal: Han Zhen then colluded to confirm the matter as true; Shizhong and Shunqing were both demoted and exiled, while Shao was made Palace Attendant and collator of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhen then colluded to confirm the matter; Shizhong and Shunqing were both demoted and exiled, while Shao was made Palace Attendant and collator of the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 後帥郭逵上韶盜貸市易錢，安石以為不足校，徙逵涇原。

translations.literal: Later commander Guo Kui memorialized that Shao had embezzled market-control funds; Anshi held it not worth investigating and transferred Kui to Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later commander Guo Kui memorialized that Shao had embezzled market-control funds; Anshi held it not worth investigating and transferred Kui to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝志復河、隴，築古渭為通遠軍，以韶知軍事。

translations.literal: The emperor was resolved to recover the He and Long regions; ancient Weizhou was fortified as Tongyuan Army, and Shao was made its military administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was resolved to recover the He and Long regions; ancient Weizhou was fortified as Tongyuan Army, and Shao was made its military administrator.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，引兵城渭源堡及乞神平，破蒙羅角、抹耳水巴等族。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year, he led troops to fortify Weiyuan Stockade and Qishenping, and defeated the Mengluojiao, Mo'ershuiba, and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year, he led troops to fortify Weiyuan Stockade and Qishenping and defeated the Mengluojiao, Mo'ershuiba, and other tribes.

sentences.zh: 初，羌保險，諸將謀置陣平地，韶曰：「賊不舍險來鬥，則我師必徒歸。

translations.literal: At first the Qiang held the defiles; the generals planned to deploy on level ground. Shao said: "If the enemy will not leave the defiles to fight, our army must return empty-handed."
translations.idiomatic: At first the Qiang held the defiles; the generals planned to deploy on level ground. Shao said, "If the enemy will not leave the defiles to fight, our army must return empty-handed."

sentences.zh: 今已入險地，當使險為吾有。

translations.literal: We have already entered dangerous ground; we must make the defiles ours.
translations.idiomatic: We have already entered dangerous ground; we must make the defiles ours.

sentences.zh: 」乃徑趣抹邦山，壓敵軍而陣，令曰：「敢言退者斬！

translations.literal: Thereupon he pressed straight for Mobang Mountain, deployed pressing against the enemy army, and ordered: "Whoever speaks of retreat shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he pressed straight for Mobang Mountain, deployed pressing against the enemy, and ordered, "Whoever speaks of retreat shall be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 」賊乘高下鬥，師小卻。

translations.literal: The enemy fought from higher ground; the army fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fought from higher ground; the army fell back slightly.

sentences.zh: 韶躬擐甲胃，麾帳下兵逆擊之，羌大潰，焚其廬帳而還，洮西大震。

translations.literal: Shao donned armor himself, commanded his personal guard to counterattack, the Qiang broke in great rout, their lodges and tents were burned, and they returned; the west of the Tao was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Shao donned armor himself, commanded his personal guard to counterattack, the Qiang broke in great rout, their lodges and tents were burned, and the west of the Tao was greatly shaken.

sentences.zh: 會瞎征度洮為之援，餘黨復集。

translations.literal: Just then Xiazheng crossed the Tao to bring reinforcements, and the remaining bands gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Xiazheng crossed the Tao to bring reinforcements, and the remaining bands gathered again.

sentences.zh: 韶命別將由竹牛嶺路張軍聲，而潛師越武勝，遇瞎征首領瞎藥等，與戰破之，遂城武勝，建為鎮洮軍。

translations.literal: Shao ordered a separate general to take the Zhuniu Ridge route to feign troop movements, while secretly leading his army over Wusheng; they encountered Xiazheng's chieftains Xiayao and others, defeated them in battle, then fortified Wusheng and established it as Zhentao Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shao ordered a separate general to take the Zhuniu Ridge route to feign troop movements while secretly leading his army over Wusheng; they encountered Xiazheng's chieftains Xiayao and others, defeated them, fortified Wusheng, and established it as Zhentao Army.

sentences.zh: 進右正言、集賢殿修撰。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Rectifier and compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Rectifier and compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 復擊走瞎征，降其部落二萬。

translations.literal: He again attacked and drove off Xiazheng, and twenty thousand of his tribes submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He again attacked and drove off Xiazheng, and twenty thousand of his tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 更名鎮洮為熙州，以熙、河、洮、岷、通遠為一路，韶以龍圖閣待制知熙州。

translations.literal: Zhentao was renamed Xizhou; Xi, He, Tao, Min, and Tongyuan were made one circuit, and Shao was made editorial acolyte of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhentao was renamed Xizhou; Xi, He, Tao, Min, and Tongyuan were made one circuit, and Shao was made editorial acolyte of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，取河州，遷樞密直學士。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year he took Hezhou and was transferred to direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year he took Hezhou and was transferred to direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 降羌叛，韶回軍擊之。

translations.literal: The submitted Qiang rebelled; Shao turned his army and struck them.
translations.idiomatic: The submitted Qiang rebelled; Shao turned his army and struck them.

sentences.zh: 瞎征以其間據河州，韶進破訶諾木藏城，穿露骨山，南入洮州境，道狹隘，釋馬徒行，或日至六七。

translations.literal: Xiazheng took advantage of the interval to seize Hezhou. Shao advanced, broke Henuomucang city, passed through Lougu Mountain, and entered Taozhou territory; the road was narrow and steep, so they abandoned their horses and went on foot, sometimes covering only six or seven li a day.
