translations.literal: On audience he was retained and appointed Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; his son Can was made judicial officer of Kaifeng to facilitate his support.
translations.idiomatic: On audience he was retained and appointed Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; his son Can was made judicial officer of Kaifeng to facilitate his support.

sentences.zh: 逾年，力謝事罷，授資政殿學士、中太一宮使，未幾，卒。

translations.literal: After a year he strenuously begged to retire and was dismissed, granted Academic Bachelor of the Hall of Zizheng and Commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he strenuously begged to retire and was dismissed, granted Academic Bachelor of the Hall of Zizheng and Commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace; before long he died.

sentences.zh: 徽宗悼之。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong mourned him.

sentences.zh: 贈右銀青光祿大夫，諡曰「莊簡」，賻恤甚厚。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Master of the Right Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, with the posthumous title "Zhuangjian," and funeral gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Master of the Right Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, with the posthumous title Zhuangjian, "Solemn and Simple," and funeral gifts were very generous.

sentences.zh: 楶七子：縡、綜、綡、綰、綖、縯、縝。

translations.literal: Jie had seven sons: Can, Zong, Gao, Wan, Yan, Yan, and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had seven sons: Can, Zong, Gao, Wan, Yan, Yan, and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 縡、綡最知名。

translations.literal: Can and Gao were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Can and Gao were the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 縡繇推官為戶部員外郎、提點淮南東路刑獄、權知揚州兼提舉香鹽事。

translations.literal: Can rose from judicial officer to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, judicial commissioner of Huainan East Circuit, and acting prefect of Yangzhou concurrently commissioner of incense and salt.
translations.idiomatic: Can rose from judicial officer to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, judicial commissioner of Huainan East Circuit, and acting prefect of Yangzhou concurrently commissioner of incense and salt.

sentences.zh: 時方鑄崇寧大錢，令下，市區晝閉，人持錢買物，至日旰，皇皇無肯售。

translations.literal: At the time Chongning large coins were being cast; when the order came down the market districts closed by day; people holding coins to buy goods found none willing to sell even until sunset.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chongning large coins were being cast; when the order came down the market districts closed by day; people holding coins to buy goods found none willing to sell even until sunset.

sentences.zh: 縡飾市易務致百貨，以小錢收之；

translations.literal: Can stocked the market-control office with all goods and collected payment in small coins;
translations.idiomatic: Can stocked the market-control office with all goods and collected payment in small coins;

sentences.zh: 且檄倉吏糶米，以大錢予之，盡十日止，民心遂安。

translations.literal: and also ordered granary clerks to sell rice and pay in large coins; this lasted ten days and then stopped, and popular sentiment was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: and also ordered granary clerks to sell rice and pay in large coins; this lasted ten days and then stopped, and popular sentiment was pacified.

sentences.zh: 未幾，新鈔法行，舊鈔盡廢，一時商賈束手，或自殺。

translations.literal: Before long the new note law was implemented and old notes were all abolished; merchants were helpless for a time, and some killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the new note law was implemented and old notes were all abolished; merchants were helpless for a time, and some killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 縡得訴者所持舊鈔，為錢以千計者三十萬，上疏言鈔法誤民，請如約以示大信。

translations.literal: Can obtained old notes held by complainants amounting to three hundred thousand in cash by the thousand; he submitted a memorial saying the note law harmed the people and begged fulfillment as promised to show great faith.
translations.idiomatic: Can obtained old notes held by complainants amounting to three hundred thousand in cash by the thousand; he submitted a memorial saying the note law harmed the people and begged fulfillment as promised to show great faith.

sentences.zh: 上怒，罷縡，降兩官。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, removed Can, and demoted him two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry, removed Can, and demoted him two ranks.

sentences.zh: 綡第進士，歷陝西轉運判官，入為戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: Gao passed the jinshi examination and served as Shaanxi transportation judicial officer; he entered as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Gao passed the jinshi examination and served as Shaanxi transportation judicial officer; he entered as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎劉逵之妻，綡姊也。

translations.literal: Chief Secretariat Vice Director Liu Kui's wife was Gao's elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretariat Vice Director Liu Kui's wife was Gao's elder sister.

sentences.zh: 逵漸復元祐之政，綡多贊之。

translations.literal: Kui gradually restored Yuanyou policies; Gao often supported him.
translations.idiomatic: Kui gradually restored Yuanyou policies; Gao often supported him.

sentences.zh: 蔡京欲擠逵，且惎綡不附己，使其黨攻之，出綡湖州。

translations.literal: Cai Jing wished to oust Kui and also resented Gao for not siding with him; he had his faction attack him and sent Gao to Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing wished to oust Kui and also resented Gao for not siding with him; he had his faction attack him and sent Gao to Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 論者不已，差主管西京崇福宮。

translations.literal: Critics would not cease; he was assigned to supervise the Western Capital Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Critics would not cease; he was assigned to supervise the Western Capital Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 綜歷通判常州，綰知丹徒縣，綖簽判西安州，縯簽判蘇州，楶孫茇承奉郎，藎監蘇州稅，俱列仕顯。

translations.literal: Zong served as vice prefect of Changzhou; Wan as magistrate of Dantu County; Yan as signing officer of Xi'an Prefecture; Yan as signing officer of Suzhou; Jie's grandson Ba as Gentleman for Palace Service; Jin as supervisor of Suzhou tax—all held visible office.
translations.idiomatic: Zong served as vice prefect of Changzhou; Wan as magistrate of Dantu County; Yan as signing officer of Xi'an Prefecture; Yan as signing officer of Suzhou; Jie's grandson Ba as Gentleman for Palace Service; Jin as supervisor of Suzhou tax—all held visible office.

sentences.zh: 及京復相，遂興制獄，傾章氏。

translations.literal: When Jing again became chief minister he then launched a fabricated prosecution to destroy the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing again became chief minister he then launched a fabricated prosecution to destroy the Zhang clan.

sentences.zh: 綖居蘇州，或得私鑄錢數巨罌，京風言者誣綖與州人郁寶所鑄。

translations.literal: Yan was living in Suzhou when someone obtained several huge jars of privately cast coin; Jing had rumor-mongers accuse Yan and a Suzhou man Yu Bao of casting them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was living in Suzhou when someone obtained several huge jars of privately cast coin; Jing had rumor-mongers accuse Yan and a Suzhou man Yu Bao of casting them.

sentences.zh: 詔遣李孝壽、張茂直、沈畸、蕭服更往鞫之，連繫數百人，累月卒無實，獄多死者。

translations.literal: An edict sent Li Xiaoshou, Zhang Maozhi, Shen Ji, and Xiao Fu in turn to investigate; several hundred were implicated; after months there was still no proof, and many died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Li Xiaoshou, Zhang Maozhi, Shen Ji, and Xiao Fu in turn to investigate; several hundred were implicated; after months there was still no proof, and many died in prison.

sentences.zh: 京大怒，別遣孫傑鞫之，傅致如章綖刺面配沙門島，追毀出身以來文字，除名勒停，籍入其家。

translations.literal: Jing was greatly angered and separately sent Sun Jie to investigate; a case was fabricated as though Zhang Yan had his face tattooed and was sent to Shamen Island; all documents since his first office were revoked, his name was struck from the rolls, and his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was greatly angered and separately sent Sun Jie to investigate; a case was fabricated as though Zhang Yan had his face tattooed and was sent to Shamen Island; all documents since his first office were revoked, his name was struck from the rolls, and his household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 竄縡台州，綜秀州，綡溫州，綰睦州，縯永州，茇處州，藎均州，官司降罷除名者十餘人，時論冤之。

translations.literal: Can was exiled to Taizhou, Zong to Xiuzhou, Gao to Wenzhou, Wan to Muzhou, Yan to Yongzhou, Ba to Chuzhou, Jin to Junzhou; more than ten officials were demoted, dismissed, and struck from the rolls; public opinion held it a great injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Can was exiled to Taizhou, Zong to Xiuzhou, Gao to Wenzhou, Wan to Muzhou, Yan to Yongzhou, Ba to Chuzhou, Jin to Junzhou; more than ten officials were demoted, dismissed, and struck from the rolls; public opinion held it a great injustice.

sentences.zh: 孫傑擢龍圖閣直學士、知蘇州，張商英入相，始辨前獄，移綖常州，綡復朝奉郎、通判秀州。

translations.literal: Sun Jie was promoted to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Suzhou; when Zhang Shangying entered as chief minister he began to review the earlier case; Yan was moved to Changzhou and Gao restored to Court Gentleman for Consultation and vice prefect of Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jie was promoted to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Suzhou; when Zhang Shangying entered as chief minister he began to review the earlier case; Yan was moved to Changzhou and Gao restored to Court Gentleman for Consultation and vice prefect of Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，綖改授內殿崇班，綡秘書省校書郎，遷戶部員外郎，出提點兩浙刑獄，以龍圖閣直學士知越州。

translations.literal: Before long Yan was reassigned as Inner Palace Attendant; Gao as collator of the Secretariat; he was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, sent out as judicial commissioner of the two Zhe circuits, and made direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yan was reassigned as Inner Palace Attendant; Gao as collator of the Secretariat; he was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, sent out as judicial commissioner of the two Zhe circuits, and made direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 譚稹宣撫燕山，請綡為參謀，加右文殿修撰。

translations.literal: Tan Zai as frontier commissioner for Yanshan requested Gao as staff officer and added him as compiler of the Hall of Youwen.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zai as frontier commissioner for Yanshan requested Gao as staff officer and added him as compiler of the Hall of Youwen.

sentences.zh: 金人破蔚州，背歸山後議，稹以錯置乖方罷。

translations.literal: When the Jurchen took Weizhou and reneged on the post-mountain agreement, Zai was removed for misplaced arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchen took Weizhou and reneged on the post-mountain agreement, Zai was removed for misplaced arrangements.

sentences.zh: 綡落職送吏部，會赦恩，上書告老，復龍圖閣直學士致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Gao was stripped of office and sent to the Ministry of Personnel; when an amnesty came he submitted a memorial begging to retire, was restored to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion and retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was stripped of office and sent to the Ministry of Personnel; when an amnesty came he submitted a memorial begging to retire, was restored to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion and retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：神宗奮英特之資，乘財力之富，銳然欲復河、湟，平靈、夏，而蔡挺、王韶、章楶輩起諸生，委褒衣，樹勳戎馬間。

translations.literal: The commentators say: Emperor Shenzong exerted extraordinary talent, possessed the wealth of fiscal strength, and was keen to recover He and Huang, pacify Ling and Xia; yet Cai Ting, Wang Shao, Zhang Jie, and their kind rose from student status, laid aside scholar's robes, and built merit amid war horses.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Emperor Shenzong exerted extraordinary talent, possessed the wealth of fiscal strength, and was keen to recover He and Huang, pacify Ling and Xia; yet Cai Ting, Wang Shao, Zhang Jie, and their kind rose from student status, laid aside scholar's robes, and built merit amid war horses.

sentences.zh: 世非無材，顧上所趣尚磨厲奚如耳。

translations.literal: The age was not without talent—it depended on what the ruler valued and how he honed it.
translations.idiomatic: The age was not without talent—it depended on what the ruler valued and how he honed it.

sentences.zh: 觀挺之治兵，韶之策敵，楶之制勝，亦一時良將。

translations.literal: Observing Ting's training of troops, Shao's strategy against the enemy, and Jie's victories—they too were fine generals of their time.
translations.idiomatic: Observing Ting's training of troops, Shao's strategy against the enemy, and Jie's victories—they too were fine generals of their time.

sentences.zh: 薛向雖無三子勞，而董漕邊饟，不乏仰給，持重樞府，不啟事端，又其善也。

translations.literal: Although Xue Xiang had not the labor of the three, he directed transport and frontier provisions without failing in supply, and in the Bureau of Military Affairs held steady without opening hostilities—that too was his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Although Xue Xiang had not the labor of the three, he directed transport and frontier provisions without failing in supply, and in the Bureau of Military Affairs held steady without opening hostilities—that too was his virtue.

sentences.zh: 若厚之降隴拶、瞎征，取湟、鄯、廓州，功足繼韶。

translations.literal: As for Hou's submission of Longzhan and Xiazheng and taking Huang, Shan, and Kuozhou—his merit was enough to continue Shao's.
translations.idiomatic: As for Hou's submission of Longzhan and Xiazheng and taking Huang, Shan, and Kuozhou—his merit was enough to continue Shao's.

sentences.zh: 而嗣昌造釁北伐，乃悖於向，可勝誅邪？

translations.literal: Yet Sichang created the provocation for the northern campaign—contrary to Xiang—can blame enough be assigned?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Sichang created the provocation for the northern campaign—contrary to Xiang—can blame enough be assigned?

sentences.zh: 雖然，佳兵好還，道家所戒，卒之寀以左道殺，綖以鑄錢陷，此非其驗也與。

translations.literal: Even so, fine weapons are fond of returning—a warning of the Daoists; in the end Cai was killed for heterodox arts and Yan was trapped by coin casting—is this not their proof?
translations.idiomatic: Even so, fine weapons are fond of returning—a warning of the Daoists; in the end Cai was killed for heterodox arts and Yan was trapped by coin casting—is this not their proof?
